• Detail-oriented, organized and able to manage multiple priorities that may be constantly changing
• Self-driven, flexible, and highly energetic with strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills
• Able to work effectively and efficiently both independently and collaboratively

• Proficient in a variety of technology systems including Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and Outlook) and ability to learn and adapt to new systems quickly

• 3+ years of restaurant or retail management experience

• Must be 18 years of age or older

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

We’re looking for a creative, culturally plugged in communications professional to join our Consumer Communications team and help shape how LinkedIn reaches new audiences.

In this role, you’ll help lead our always-on consumer storytelling and partnerships work across the U.S., finding creative ways to bring LinkedIn into conversations happening beyond traditional business and workplace media. You’ll identify cultural moments where LinkedIn has something relevant to say, develop relationships with talent, media and emerging platforms, and build partnerships that introduce LinkedIn to new audiences.

The right person is equal parts storyteller, relationship builder and operator. You have strong instincts for what people are talking about, where conversations are happening and how a brand can participate in a way that feels relevant rather than forced. You’re comfortable moving quickly from an idea to execution, building relationships with media and external partners, and collaborating across cross-functional partners like, marketing, social, editorial and product.

Our customers are the companies responsible for moving the materials that power the real economy; electrical supplies, plumbing products, roofing materials, HVAC equipment, and more. Every day, thousands of people rely on Canals to help process orders, manage purchasing, handle accounts payable, and streamline critical business workflows.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Comfortable juggling multiple projects and shifting timelines

We're building software that solves real problems for an industry that keeps the world running. Our customers rely on our platform every day to operate their businesses.

We've found strong product-market fit and continue to grow quickly, creating opportunities for people who want to have a meaningful impact on the trajectory of a company.

• Review and comment on construction and disbursement schedules as well as other submitted documents including but not limited to:
• Zoning approvals
• Certified surveys
• Building permit approvals
• Utility company approval letters
• Soil and foundation engineering reports
• Designer's certification of code and ADA compliance.
• Prepare Construction Risk Assessment Reports.
• Other duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or related field.
• Two to Five plus (2- 5) years of engineering, construction management, or architecture.
• Two to Five plus (2- 5) of water and wastewater experience preferred.

Preferred Skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Strong organizational and analytical skills.
• Knowledge of critical path method scheduling.
• Experience using project management information systems for managing projects.
• Ability to provide efficient, timely, reliable and courteous service to customers.

jobs.title: Manager, Programmatic Strategy
jobs.location: New York, NEW YORK, United States
jobs.description:
The Manager, Programmatic Strategy will report to the Director of Programmatic Strategy and will play a key role in shaping and executing NBCUniversal’s broader programmatic business strategy across demand and supply.

This role will be instrumental at helping future proof NBCU’s programmatic advertising business and will be very collaborative – working regularly with sales, ad operations, product, and planning teams.

Responsibilities

• Own and develop programmatic business strategy across demand, supply, monetization, marketplace opportunities, translating business priorities and market trends into actionable strategies.
• Identify and evaluate growth opportunities across the programmatic ecosystem, including new partnerships, products, identify solutions, signals, deal types, monetization opportunities.
• Analyze business and partner performance to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and areas for optimization; develop clear recommendations and communicate key insights to the strategy team.
• Assist in day-to-day relationship for DSPs & SSPs for programmatic initiatives.
• Recommend and evaluate new revenue opportunities to enrich and optimize programmatic inventory.
• Tracking performance and surfacing analysis/insights for new product launches.
• Stay abreast to new developments within the broader media and advertising technology industry and within NBCUniversal’s ad tech ecosystem.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
• 5+ years’ experience directly working in programmatic at a leading corporation, agency, technology platform and/or management consulting firm
• Expert Excel user, working with large datasets, consolidating data from multiple sources, writing nested IF formulas
• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to present results of complex analyses clearly.
• Strong PowerPoint skills and proven proficiency summarizing information/analyses into coherent and concise slides.
• Must possess a passion for media and strong intellectual curiosity

Desired Characteristics

• Strong foundational understanding of advertising sales, advanced advertising and the programmatic marketplace.
• Superior attention to detail in analytical insights, written reports, emails, and PowerPoint presentations
• Strong organizational skills – ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines
• Highly collaborative and adaptive to change in fast-paced environment
• Passionate about the television, ad tech, and digital media space

Hybrid: This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
Based in Houston, Texas, you’ll provide high-level confidential administrative and business support to the CEO of Government Medical Services. Your work will span executive calendar management, international travel, Board and leadership meeting support, action tracking, correspondence, office administration, and coordination across multiple time zones.

Key Responsibilities

• Manage the CEO’s schedule, workload, meetings, contacts, and priorities, ensuring appropriate preparation, briefing materials, agendas, and follow-up actions are completed.
• Coordinate complex domestic and international travel, including flights, accommodations, ground transportation, visas, itineraries, and travel expense reporting.
• Support Board members and senior executives by coordinating meetings and corporate events, preparing materials, managing logistics, recording minutes, and maintaining action trackers.
• Prepare executive-level correspondence, presentations, reports, meeting notes, and Board reporting materials while maintaining accurate records and documentation.
• Provide highly confidential administrative support involving sensitive business and personal information, including selected travel, visa, residency, and passport-related support for the CEO’s family.
• Manage administrative activities for the Houston office while coordinating effectively with colleagues and stakeholders across an international organization.

If you’re at your best when anticipating what an executive will need, keeping complex priorities moving, and handling sensitive matters with sound judgment and discretion, this role provides that level of responsibility.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree from a recognized institution.
• Minimum 5 years’ experience in a similar Executive Assistant role within a multinational company supporting at C-level.
• Demonstrated experience managing complex domestic and international travel and taking minutes at Board-level meetings.
• Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and SharePoint; strong Excel skills; working knowledge of Visio and Project; and strong, developing AI skills.
• Excellent written and spoken English, with strong interpersonal and customer service skills and the ability to communicate effectively with employees and senior stakeholders at all levels.
• Demonstrated ability to manage confidential matters, data protection requirements, and executive privacy with discretion; willingness to travel approximately 10% of the time.

Preferred

• Experience in business support functions such as Human Resources or Sales Support.
• Experience working with non-U.S. companies and supporting business activities across international environments.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Privacy Disclaimer: Policy Link

As a Research Intern for World-Action Models / VLA for Autonomous Driving, you contribute to research projects at the forefront of the ADAS/AD industry. You will work at the intersection of VLAs, generative modeling and world models, and contribute to research that pushes toward scalable autonomy. Key responsibilities include:

• Designing and training world-action models (autoregressive / diffusion-based) that predict future sensor observations or latent states conditioned on ego actions.
• Integrating world models with planning for end-to-end or model-based driving policies.

You will collaborate closely with other researchers, and strong work is expected to lead to top-venue publications and/or product impact.

Basic Qualifications

• Ph.D. student in Computer Science, Robotics, Computer Engineering, or a related field (must be a currently enrolled student).
• Minimum GPA of 3.0
• Hands-on experience with at least one of: generative models (diffusion, autoregressive transformers, VAEs), world models / video prediction, or end-to-end autonomous driving.
• Solid fine-tuning skills and proficiency with deep learning frameworks.
• Experience with reinforcement learning and/or model-based planning.

Preferred Qualifications

• Publication record in top venues including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR, NeurIPS and ICML.
• Familiarity with driving benchmarks such as NavSim and Bench2Drive.
• Experience with large-scale distributed training and multi-modal / video data pipelines.
• Able to work independently, with strong research and problem-solving skills.
• Good communication and teamwork skills.

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans

jobs.title: Industrial & Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Our Story
Powering fast, reliable fulfillment for Adorama, Scuba.com and Sunny Sports, the shipping warehouse is the backbone of our e-commerce business. Distributing from two warehouses, we ensure that creators, adventurers, and enthusiasts alike get the gear they need—accurately and on time.

Whether it’s camera equipment, dive gear, or outdoor essentials, our warehouse teams handle every step of the process with precision, care, and a deep commitment to the customer experience. We don’t just ship products—we help deliver moments of inspiration, exploration, and creativity.

We’re a team that takes pride in doing things right—working together to ensure every package that leaves our warehouses reflects the quality, reliability, and service our customers expect from each of our brands.

Our Leadership Principles

• Growth Mindset: We set high standards, embrace failure, and are open to change.

• Be Customer-Centered: We focus on the end-to-end customer experience.

• Take Ownership & Dig Deeper: We are proactive, use data, and avoid shortcuts.

• Think Like a Start-Up: We move fast, stay flexible, and celebrate every win.

• Be Humble & Respectful: We assume positive intent, listen actively, and support one another.

Position Summary

Lead industrial engineering and warehouse automation initiatives to improve productivity, labor utilization, material flow and fulfillment capacity. A central responsibility is to help Adorama successfully implement, integrate and maximize the long-term value of its Goods-to-Person (GTP) system. The role also develops the labor standards, planning models, performance reporting and process improvements needed across manual and automated operations. This is a hands-on position requiring strong analytical judgment, independent project leadership and regular involvement on the warehouse floor.

Key Responsibilities

• GTP implementation and performance: Represent Fulfillment in GTP design reviews, process validation, integration planning, installation readiness, testing, commissioning and operational handover; monitor vendor deliverables and project milestones.

• GTP capacity and ROI: Challenge and validate assumptions for throughput, presentation rates, staffing, labor savings, utilization and system capacity; establish baselines and compare actual results with committed performance after go-live.

• Labor planning and performance engineering: Develop engineered labor standards, workload-to-hours models, staffing forecasts and actionable daily/weekly KPIs by building, department and process; explain performance changes using output and actual labor hours.

• Data and reporting: Convert existing WMS/AS400, Looker and operational data into practical management tools; partner with BI and IT on data quality, dashboard development and automation of recurring analysis.

• Process improvement: Observe and measure receiving, putaway, replenishment, picking, packing, sorting and shipping; identify bottlenecks, waste and variation; test improvements and quantify before-and-after results.

• Material and order flow: Optimize slotting, hot zones, batching, order routing, replenishment, work release and movement between manual processes and automated equipment while protecting shipping cutoffs.

• Automation integration and reliability: Work with IT, vendors, Operations and Maintenance on WMS/WCS interfaces, equipment performance, recurring faults and root-cause analysis; recommend corrective actions and verify results.

• Cross-functional project delivery: Lead assigned engineering initiatives, track owners and deadlines, evaluate vendors and capital proposals, communicate risks and results, and support future capacity and network planning.

Working Relationships & Accountability

• Report directly to the VP of Fulfillment; partner closely with the Sr. Director of Operations, Senior Operations Manager, department leaders, BI/IT, Maintenance and external automation partners.

• Engineer owns analytical methods, standards, process design recommendations and validation of results; Operations leadership owns daily staffing, execution, coaching and sustained performance.

• Influence change through data, practical floor-level collaboration and clear recommendations, without relying on direct supervisory authority.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent directly relevant experience.

• 4+ years of hands-on industrial/operations engineering experience in a high-volume distribution or e-commerce fulfillment environment; demonstrated ability to work independently.

• Proven experience with labor standards, productivity analysis, staffing or capacity models, and measurable warehouse process improvements.

• Practical experience with automated material handling systems and understanding of WMS/WCS-driven workflows, system interfaces and material flow.

• Strong analytical skills using Excel and operational datasets; ability to work with BI/reporting tools and translate findings into clear actions for operating leaders.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects and working effectively with vendors, IT, maintenance and warehouse teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct GTP, AS/RS, sortation or similar warehouse automation implementation and ramp-up experience.

• Experience with AS400/IBM i, Looker, SQL or other warehouse reporting and analysis tools.

• Lean Six Sigma, PMP or similar continuous improvement/project management credentials; experience supporting capital ROI and acceptance testing.

Measures of Success

• GTP launch readiness, achieved throughput, utilization and verified benefits versus approved design assumptions.

• Accurate, usable labor planning models and timely visibility into productivity drivers at department and process levels.

• Documented productivity, quality, labor efficiency and material-flow improvements with measurable before-and-after results.

• Effective project delivery, cross-functional adoption and sustainable operating processes.

jobs.title: Customer Sucess Manager III - Dallas, TX
jobs.description:
OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com http://OpenGov.com.




JOB SUMMARY

As a Customer Success Manager III at OpenGov, you are a strategic architect of customer value. You will own a dedicated portfolio of ~40 high-impact customers, serving as their primary long-term partner tasked with understanding their unique goals, challenges &  workflows. This is a senior-level role for a CSM who excels at navigating complex political landscapes, driving process transformation, and securing long-term retention through measurable business outcomes. You won't just manage accounts; you will influence the digital transformation of modern government.

 
 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Strategic Portfolio Leadership: Own the end-to-end success strategy for ~40 customers, aligning OpenGov’s platform with their specific legislative goals and operational challenges.

 - Executive Advisory: Build and nurture deep relationships with Department Heads, City Managers, and Finance Directors, acting as a trusted advisor to drive high retention and platform stickiness.

 - Complex Change Management: Guide customers through significant process changes, leveraging industry best practices to ensure deep product adoption and workflow optimization.

 - Business Impact Reporting: Design and deliver high-impact Executive Business Reviews (EBRs) that translate usage data into tangible value and ROI for stakeholders.

 - Retention & Growth: Proactively monitor portfolio health to mitigate churn risk and identify expansion opportunities that align with the customer’s long-term roadmap.

 - Adoption & Value Consulting: Be able to design programs to maximize the adoption of OpenGov across your customers, resulting in a measurable increase in value.

 - Cross-Functional Advocacy: Partner with Sales, Product, and Support teams to resolve complex roadblocks and ensure the "Voice of the Customer" informs our future product development.

 - Process Innovation: Contribute to the "playbook." As a CSM III, you’ll help build our workflows for churn prevention and onboarding efficiency.

 
 


REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - SaaS Expertise: Minimum of 3–5 years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related high-touch SaaS role.

 - Proven Track Record: Demonstrated ability to manage complex customer relationships, hit high Net Revenue Retention (NRR) targets, and drive revenue growth.

 - Strategic Thinking: A customer-centric mindset with the ability to move between high-level strategy and tactical execution.

 - Advanced Communication: Exceptional presentation and interpersonal skills, specifically the ability to command a room of executive-level decision-makers.

 - Technical Proficiency: Willingness to be hands-on in product; Mastery of CRM and CS tools such as Salesforce, Gong, or Gainsight.

 - Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field.

 - Industry Context: Previous experience in GovTech or working directly with government agencies is highly preferred.

 - Travel: Willingness and ability to travel to meet with key customers in person (approx. 25-30%).




COMPENSATION 

Dallas, TX: $105,000 - $120,000



On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

 

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

 




WHY OPENGOV?



A Mission That Matters. 

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust.  Some people say this is boring.  We think it’s the core of our democracy.



Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.



A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.



A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.



Benefits That Work for You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

 - Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families

 - Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions

 - Professional development and growth opportunities

 - A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

We are looking for enthusiastic individuals to join our team as Behavior Technicians. As a Behavior Technician, you will have the opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of children with autism.

In this role, you will work one-on-one with children, implementing individualized behavior intervention plans under the guidance of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). You will use evidence-based techniques to teach communication, social, and daily living skills while reducing interfering behaviors.

Our clients move, so you need to be comfortable standing, walking, sitting, grasping, reaching, bending, kneeling, crouching, squatting, lifting, and at times carrying children or objects that weigh up to 50 pounds.

At the end of each day, you will go home knowing that you have made a meaningful impact on the life of a child and their family. Join us and become a part of a dedicated team that is changing lives for the better. Apply now to start your journey as a Behavior Technician with us!

For more information, visit www.braskem.com/usa.

Department: Maintenance

Location: Freeport, TX

Travel Involved: Less than 5%

Job Type: Full-time

Description:

The Maintenance Planner role within MPE is responsible for the duties listed below for mechanical planning activities. Planning requires a detailed job package for each task and resource involved in completing a work order, as assigned by the Production Maintenance Coordinator (PMC) or the planner’s immediate supervisor.

Key Responsibilities Include:

• Review each day the notifications prioritized by the PMC to determine which jobs are to be planned.

• Process work notifications and work orders properly, ensuring status codes are correct

• Discuss and understand the notification scope, interacting with the notification issuer and/or maintenance craftsmen to understand history, deficiencies, special requirements, and possible initial troubleshooting

• Create Work Orders from Work Notifications, using appropriate codes for the type of work, such as maint work center.

• Visit the job site and scope out the job by taking pictures, creating drawings and sketches, and assembling a bill of materials. Walking down the job with a craftsman may be required.

• Enter plans into maintenance work orders by developing, within each one, a well-defined list of tasks with an adequately detailed scope of work, including all necessary steps to perform each task and complete the work order.

• Develop special instructions and provide the required documentation, such as MOC, QA/QC forms, data sheets, and piping schematics.

• Create and review Task Lists within SAP to be used for future work

• Request materials, parts, and services, as appropriate, for the maintenance work

• Inform engineers of Add/Change/Delete needs for spare parts that must be managed by procurement or kept in inventory. Also inform when parts aren’t tied to equipment BOM in SAP.

• Review feedback form from Maintenance Technicians, Engineers, etc. on the plans that have been executed or attempted

• Work with the contractor administrator by issuing requisitions for outside contractors on planned jobs so he can issue them PO’s.

• Support, when needed, in issuing POs or SESs for emergency work involving outside contractors.

Preferred Skills, Education, and Experience:

• High school diploma or GED required.

• Associate degree in Industrial Technology, Mechanical Technology, Engineering Technology, or related field preferred.

• Minimum 5 years of industrial maintenance experience, OR

• Minimum 3 years of maintenance planning experience in a manufacturing, chemical, refinery, power generation, or petrochemical facility.

• Experience planning mechanical, piping, rotating equipment, or fixed equipment work.

• Working knowledge of: Pumps Gearboxes Motors Heat exchangers Piping systems Valves Compressors Preventive and predictive maintenance programs

• Ability to read and interpret: P&IDs Equipment drawings Mechanical drawings Isometric drawings Technical manuals

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Data Platforms
jobs.description:
Summary

Wikipedia and its sister projects are among the most popular media properties in the world, visited by over 1 billion people a month across over 300 different languages. These sites generate a tremendous amount of data on how people learn and collaborate.  The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a group product manager to guide the development and evolution of our data platforms, the collection of technologies we use to understand how Wikipedia works, improve its experiences, and spread free knowledge.

The group product manager is a leader in the strategic decision-making and tactical execution for the Data Engineering, Experimentation, Search, and Data Platform Site Reliability teams. This role shares leadership responsibility with the Director of Engineering for Data Platform Engineering, and works in collaboration with data analysts, researchers, and product teams building user-facing features for reading and editing Wikipedia on the web and mobile apps. This is a people management role, managing two individually-contributing product managers.

In this role, you and your group of product managers will guide the evolution of our data pipelines, data lake, experiment platform, and analytics tools.  This includes ingestion, orchestration, computation, and serving data using a variety of technologies such as Kafka, Flink, Hadoop, Spark, Airflow, Iceberg, Kubernetes, Superset, dbt, and OpenSearch. A strong candidate will have deep experience building a data platform to serve product analytics and production needs, and be technically conversant in the relevant technologies.

This position will report to the Senior Director of Product, Core Experiences.

Candidates must be available for critical meetings and synchronous work between 15:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC, and open to traveling internationally up to four times per year.

This role is accountable for:

• Ensuring the accuracy, usefulness, reliability, and accessibility of our data products

• Defining and setting priorities and roadmaps for Data Platform Engineering teams across four domains: data engineering, search, experimentation, and site reliability

• Product lifecycle management of the products, services, and tools of the Data Platform Engineering teams

• Co-developing product strategy, providing leadership, and making and facilitating sound decisions

• Managing and developing a team of product managers

• Partnering with user-facing product teams to use the data platform to guide product decisions and build derived-data products

Expected skills and experience include:

• Minimum of 5 years of product management experience with data or infrastructure products

• Experience hiring and managing product managers

• Success delivering data and analytical products and services depended on by multiple product teams

• Expertise in data analytics, A/B testing, search, and data architecture

• Strong understanding of modern techniques for handling high-scale data

• Knowledge of search technologies

• Experience navigating privacy issues around data collection, retention, and distribution

• Ability to work with multiple stakeholder teams to deliver results through lateral influence and collaboration

Qualities that are important to us:

• Commitment to the mission and values of the Wikimedia Foundation

• Effective at asynchronous communication in a distributed workplace

• Able to navigate and make decisions in circumstances with limited, incomplete, and conflicting information

• Focus on iterative delivery and minimum viability to provide value to customer teams

• Effective at clear, written communication for strategy, plans, roadmaps, and decisions, for a wide range of audiences including individual contributor engineers, volunteer contributors, and department leadership

Additionally, we would love it if you have:

• Experience with open source, open data, or open knowledge communities

• Experience building products for multiple languages and geographies.

• Experience with the integration of machine learning or artificial intelligence into web products.

• Experience editing Wikipedia or with the Wikipedia, Wikidata, or Wikimedia Commons communities or other collaborative enterprises

• Open source software development experience

• Familiarity with MediaWiki

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate against any person based upon their race, traits historically associated with race, religion, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy or related medical conditions, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristics.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$131,926 to US$206,302 with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. jobs.title: Quantum R&D Engineer – Processor Development
jobs.description:
ABOUT US 


QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in! 



We are seeking a Senior Quantum R&D Engineer to join our Quantum Processor team and develop the next generation of Quantum Processing Units (QPU). This role is focused on improving processor performance by designing, validating and iterating on-chip architectures like inter-qubit couplers and readout architectures. You will take ownership of the end-to-end development cycle, creating designs, collaborating with our fabrication teams and performing cryogenic measurement to inform design iterations. You will directly contribute these improvements into our large-scale QPUs.



What you’ll be doing

 - Design & Simulate: Conceive, model, and layout next-generation, large-scale superconducting quantum processor architectures. Design custom test vehicles and prototypes to compare and validate new component implementations (like inter-qubit couplers and readout architectures), before integrating them into full-scale processors.

 - Measure & Validate: Close the feedback loop by designing and performing cryogenic measurements on your own designs to validate performance and inform design improvements.

 - Ownership: Take complete ownership of device or component development – from the initial concept through design, simulation, experiment, data analysis, and iteration.

 - Automate: Write and improve code to automate design, simulation, and measurement workflows.

 - Collaborate: Collaborate closely with design and measurement engineers,  teams to ensure rapid design-to-test cycles



Your Profile

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience in multi-qubit superconducting quantum device development

 - Deep understanding of cQED, quantum microwave circuits and superconducting qubits.

 - Extensive experience in design and cryogenic measurement of superconducting qubit circuits

 - Proficiency in Python and software tools for quantum design and experiments (e.g. HFSS, Comsol, pyEPR, scqubits, Quantum Metal, KLayout, etc.)

 - A proactive, detail-oriented mindset with a strong drive to scale quantum technology

 - You thrive in a collaborative environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection. 

What We Offer:

At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect:

Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance)

Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage.

Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time

Personal growth - We invest in your L&D, with a budget available to each team member, dependent on their individual ambitions, development needs, and performance

A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer

Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare

We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. We know this helps us make better decisions, drives more innovation, and strengthens our culture.

About the role

As Head of TechOps Regional Execution, US, you will lead Manufacturing & Supply and CMC Science & Technology activities across Sobi’s US external CMO/CLO network. You will be accountable for reliable, compliant, on time supply from manufacturers, laboratories, packaging sites and warehouses well connected with the full global supply chain and in line with global standards and strategies.

Leading a regional organization of approximately 10 -30 FTEs, you will connect global strategy with strong regional execution, build effective supplier partnerships and drive operational improvement. The role reports to the Head of Technical Operations. Preferred location: Raleigh-Durham area, but we are open to other locations as long as you are willing to frequently travel to our offices.

What you will do

You will lead and be accountable for the regional team responsible for delivering the activities below. Your role is to set direction and priorities, empower the team and ensure effective execution and result but also support and execute operational activities and take a hands-on approach when needed.

• Lead and empower the team to deliver regional Manufacturing & Supply and Science & Technology execution in line with global strategies, plans and standards, and to act as the regional Manufacturing & Supply counterpart to relevant Sobi functions.
• Hold the team accountable for ensuring reliable on-time, in-full (OTIF) delivery across US regional suppliers, CMOs, CLOs, packaging sites and warehouses, including follow-up, issue resolution and escalation.
• Work closely with global and other regional TechOps functions to secure compliant, reliable and cost-effective supply to rare disease patients in all Sobi’s markets Globally.
• Monitor and improve regional KPIs across supply, quality, compliance, cost, productivity and technical performance, and reports results and corrective actions to Global Functions.
• Build strong partnerships with regional suppliers and manage day-to-day operational relationships within global supplier governance, provide Science & Technology support and mobilize technical expertise to resolve CMO/CLO issues.
• Partner with local QA and CMC Regulatory to deliver compliant, robust supply from manufacturers and laboratories, supports deviation investigations and provides technical assessments of change controls and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
• Monitors and trend process and analytical-method data to identify technical risks, improvement opportunities and development or optimization needs.
• Provide direction and oversight as the team runs regional Virtual Plant Teams and leads or participates in regional manufacturing and supply projects, including tech transfers and product-launch activities.
• Ensure the team represents regional CMO/CLO needs, constraints and opportunities in global decision-making, escalates material supply risks, and communicates technical risks, requirements and development or optimization needs to Global CMC Science & Technology.
• Optimize regional resource deployment and prioritization across solid-line and dotted-line resources within global governance
• Attract, develop and retain regional talent, champion the Sobi Values and foster a connected, accountable “One TechOps” culture.

About you

You are a strategic and hands-on TechOps leader who creates clarity in complex environments, builds trusted partnerships and turns priorities into action. You lead with ownership, urgency and partnership.

What you bring

• 10+ years of pharmaceutical or biotech experience across technical operations, manufacturing and supply.
• Proven leadership of high-performing teams in complex, cross-functional and international organizations.
• Strong experience in external manufacturing, supplier management and virtual plant networks, including CMOs, CDMOs, CLOs and 3PLs.
• Solid knowledge of cGMP, quality and regulatory requirements, clinical and commercial manufacturing, and technical lifecycle management.
• Clear communication, strong analytical judgment and confident decision-making.
• Fluent English; Spanish and/or Portuguese is an advantage.

Compensation and Total Rewards at Sobi

At Sobi, we are dedicated to providing our employees with a comprehensive and industry-competitive total rewards package. Our compensation philosophy is designed to recognize and reward talent, ensuring that your contributions are valued and reflected in your overall rewards.

Your total compensation at Sobi goes beyond just your base salary and annual bonus. It also includes a robust suite of benefits, such as:

• A competitive 401(k) match to support your financial future.
• Tuition and wellness reimbursements to invest in your personal and professional growth.
• A comprehensive medical, dental, and vision package to prioritize your health and well-being.
• Additional recognition awards to celebrate your achievements.

The base salary range for this role is $250,000 - $290,000. Each individual offer will be determined based on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, and location. Additionally, this role is eligible for both short-term and long-term bonuses, as outlined in the plan details.

All Sobi employees need to demonstrate behaviors in line with Sobi's core values: Care, Ambition, Urgency, Ownership and Partnership. Are you ready to be on the Sobi team? Come join a culture that empowers every person to be the person that makes a difference for rare disease.

Why Join Us?

We are a global company with over 1,900 employees in more than 30 countries and are committed to the societies where we operate. With a deeply skilled management team directing our day-to-day wins, and a Board with a stellar track record, we’re ready to take on the world’s diseases, ailments and adversity. Our people believe they have the power to make a positive impact in others’ lives because that’s exactly what we do here. If you’re seeking a career that taps into your talents in a way that makes the world a better, healthier place, we just may have a job for you.

We know our employees are our most valuable asset, and our culture conveys that. We offer a competitive benefits package, to support the health and happiness of our staff.

Sobi Culture

At Sobi, we refuse to accept the status quo. This is because we have witnessed first-hand the challenges facing those affected by rare diseases, and have used this knowledge to shape our business to find new ways of helping them.

As a specialized biopharmaceutical company, we are dedicated to rare diseases. And we see this focus as a strength. By effectively turning our research into ground-breaking treatments, we help make medicine more accessible and open up more possibilities for patients and more opportunities for those caring for them. This has been our approach since day one, but we know we can’t change the world of rare diseases on our own. Accomplishing this requires strong partnerships with patients, partners and stakeholders across the entire value chain. Together, we define how our business can create solutions that serve the needs of those affected by rare diseases while facilitating sustainable growth.

An Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re leading the way in redefining the workwear category. Our mission is to engineer better boots and apparel for our country’s tradesmen and women by working directly with real workers to learn what they actually need to execute their jobs.

The BRUNT team is not only devoted to improving on the old workwear standards, but we’re also creating a community that tradesmen and women can call their own. From our weekly hangouts at the BRUNT Garage, to hosting events across the country, we’re all about getting boots on the ground and building something real with the BRUNT crew.

How You’ll Do:

The Retention Marketing Manager owns BRUNT’s lifecycle marketing program across our owned channels, SMS and Email, building the flows and segmentation logic that move customers through the full lifecycle: from list growth (including on-site acquisition) through first purchase, repeat purchase, and long-term loyalty. You architect multi-step, conditional customer journeys with DTC revenue, repeat & cross-category behavior, and customer lifetime value (LTV) as your north star metrics. You’re also responsible for the broader health of these channels: deliverability, audience growth, engagement, and conversion. You lead and develop our Email Marketing Associate, setting priorities and raising the bar on execution.

You own day-to-day production and ideate on new flow touchpoints, driving each from concept to execution to reporting and optimization. You’re both creative and data-driven, obsessed with personalization, know how to trust but verify, thrive in a fast-paced environment, adapt quickly, and are committed to getting things done.

How You’ll Do It:

Channel Management

• Lead the hands-on build of SMS and Email flows directly in Klaviyo & Postscript, partnering with the creative team on execution and QA.

• Manage, coach, and develop the Email Marketing Associate (direct report): set priorities, review builds and QA, and grow their skills.

• Own the A/B testing program across campaigns and flows, using past performance data to guide copy and design decisions and reporting results internally each month.

• Build and maintain advanced customer segments from behavioral, transactional, and lifecycle data (RFM, purchase history, engagement, product/category affinity) to power segment-specific messaging.

• Own on-site capture and list growth for both channels, including Klaviyo and Postscript sign-up forms and pop-ups.

Retention Strategy

• Develop and present monthly Email and SMS communication plans aligned with inventory, promotions, and the master marketing calendar, prioritizing the campaign types that consistently drive revenue and brand engagement.

• Collaborate with Customer Insights to improve customer data capture and feed it into segmentation.

• Drive repeat purchase and LTV growth by designing targeted, behavior-triggered messaging and cross-category shopping campaigns.

Platform & Data Management

• Serve as the in-house Klaviyo & Postscript expert, owning flow architecture, list/segment hygiene, and deliverability configuration without relying on outside developers or agencies.

• Understand how customer and order data moves between systems (Shopify, Klaviyo, Postscript, Rivo) - custom properties, events, and integration syncs and troubleshoot when data or triggers break.

• Ensure Email and SMS compliance with CAN-SPAM and TCPA requirements managing consent capture, opt-out processing, and quiet hours adherence to protect deliverability and limit brand risk.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Lead cross-functional alignment across Acquisition, Operations, Product, Creative, eCommerce, Analytics, and Loyalty teams to coordinate promotional campaigns, product launches, and brand messaging.

• Partner with Analytics to monitor customer behavior trends and maintain internal performance dashboards.

Measurement

• Track and analyze Email/SMS performance metrics (click rate, conversion, and revenue) to measure contribution to corporate KPIs.

• Monitor customer lifetime value (LTV), retention curves, and cohort-level performance (repeat purchase rates, cross-category penetration) to map lifecycle progression.

What You Need to Succeed:

• 4+ years of hands-on retention/lifecycle marketing experience at a DTC ecommerce brand (Shopify strongly preferred), with demonstrated ownership of building (not just briefing) Email and SMS programs

• 1+ years managing and developing direct reports

• 2+ years of deep, hands-on experience building in Klaviyo, plus hands-on experience with Postscript (or a comparable platform such as Attentive) - you can independently build and debug complex, multi-step flows, including conditional splits/if-then branching logic, dynamic content, and API-based triggers, without relying on a developer

• Comfortable writing basic HTML/CSS and Liquid templating logic (if/else conditional blocks) to personalize content within a single template

• Strong Excel skills - comfortable building pivot tables, blending data from multiple exports, and turning raw performance data into clean reports and dashboards for leadership

• Strong command of customer segmentation and data: comfortable building dynamic segments from behavioral and transactional data (RFM, LTV, purchase/engagement history) and mapping them to differentiated content paths

• Familiarity with data integrations between an ESP/CDP and ecommerce platforms (Shopify) - custom properties, event tracking, and basic troubleshooting when syncs or triggers break; SQL or other data-querying skills a plus

• Track record of designing A/B tests and turning the results into program changes

• Adept in strategic thinking & analytics with a passion for innovation and creative problem solving (familiarity using tools such as Google Analytics, Looker a plus)

• Ability to commute to the office in Wilmington, MA 4 days per week

In accordance with applicable salary transparency laws, we are providing the good-faith salary range for this position. This range reflects the base salary that we reasonably expect to pay for this position at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered will depend on factors such as qualifications, experience, skills, and budget.

Benefits & Perks:

• Healthcare: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance options.

• Retirement: 401(k) plan with Company Match.

• Paid Time Off: 15 days of PTO, plus 11 paid holidays and sick leave.

• Incentives: Performance-based bonus eligibility and Equity if applicable.

The anticipated salary range for this role is:

Compensation

$95,000—$115,000 USD

No matter what experience you have within our industry we encourage you to apply. At BRUNT, we believe that a strong crew is assembled with people from different backgrounds.

We look for individuals who thrive on challenges, will be passionate about our brand, and believe that teamwork is necessary for success. Show us how your experiences have shaped you and how you can contribute to BRUNT. We can’t wait to hear from you!

jobs.title: Manager, Development Prospect Research, Development
jobs.description:
About the role:

The Manager, Development Prospect Research plays a vital role in advancing Vera’s ambitious fundraising goals by managing and strengthening our prospect identification, research, and qualification strategies across institutional, major, and principal giving and strategic board development. This role supports frontline fundraisers by delivering strategic insight and timely analysis to build and advance a dynamic pipeline of funders aligned with Vera’s mission.

Working closely with the Development and Executive teams, this position leads the development of tools and processes that ensure prospect data is well-curated, actionable, and integrated into the department’s broader strategy.

1. Prospect Identification and Research

• Lead prospect identification, qualification, and due diligence efforts for individual, foundation, and corporate donors.

• Conduct and synthesize research on philanthropic capacity, affinity, giving history, networks, and engagement opportunities to support fundraising strategy.

• Develop clear, actionable prospect profiles, briefing materials, and strategic recommendations for development leadership, executive staff, and board engagement.

• Proactively identify and prioritize high-potential prospects through wealth screening, database analysis, and external research tools.

• Provide research support for donor meetings, events, board recruitment, and other strategic engagement opportunities.

2. Strategy and Collaboration

• Partner with frontline fundraisers, development leadership, and program staff to align prospect strategy with fundraising and organizational priorities.

• Provide strategic recommendations on donor capacity, inclination, and engagement opportunities to inform cultivation and solicitation efforts.

• Proactively share prospect intelligence, relationship insights, and emerging funding opportunities with key stakeholders.

• Lead targeted prospecting initiatives to identify new donors aligned with priority programs, geographies, and fundraising goals.

3. Systems and Tools Development

• Develop and optimize research systems, workflows, and data management practices to improve efficiency, consistency, and data quality.

• Partner with Development Operations to maintain accurate prospect data, ratings, and relationship intelligence within the CRM.

• Evaluate and recommend research tools, subscriptions, and vendors, and train staff on prospect research methodologies and best practices.

• Lead relationship-mapping and network analysis initiatives while staying current on emerging trends, technologies, and practices in prospect research and philanthropy.

4. Portfolio and Pipeline Management

• Lead efforts to build, assess, and sustain a diverse, high-quality pipeline of prospective donors.

• Partner with fundraisers and leadership to develop and optimize prospect portfolios based on capacity, affinity, and readiness.

• Oversee prospect ratings, wealth screening, moves management, and research tracking to support portfolio growth and fundraising performance.

• Analyze donor and prospect trends and establish policies and practices that strengthen pipeline management, data integrity, and fundraising effectiveness.

What qualifications are we looking for?

Required:

• Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of relevant experience. In lieu of degree requirement, applicable work or life experience may be considered.

• 5+ years of experience in development prospect research, donor intelligence, or related nonprofit fundraising roles.

• Expertise with donor research methodology and practice, including wealth indicators and data analysis.

• Experience with a broad range of subscription research tools.

Preferred:

• Strong communicator, able to collaborate across teams and present findings in a concise, compelling way.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you'll bring:

• Ability to synthesize large amounts of information and provide analysis.

• Resourcefulness in pursuing knowledge.

• Highly organized, detail-oriented and adept at follow-up while working effectively to meet deliverable due dates.

• Demonstrated initiative, resourcefulness, and problem-solving skills.

• Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively.

• Strong communication skills, both oral and written.

• Committed to protecting donor data and sensitive or proprietary information.

• Willingness to learn new systems and technology.

• Committed to Vera’s mission of advancing justice and equity, and you bring a lens of inclusion and cultural competency to your work.

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and enjoy building systems that support strategy and growth.

• Drives learning and professional growth in prospect development and philanthropy.

Location:

Please note this role will report to our Washington, DC office. Vera employees adhere to a hybrid schedule and are in-office on an alternating schedule that generally amounts to 10 days per month.

Compensation and Benefits:

The compensation range for this position is $100,000 - $105,000.  Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience and performance. The salary range listed is just one component of Vera Institute’s total compensation package for employees. As an employer of choice in our field, supporting Vera staff - both personally and professionally - is a priority. To do this, we invest in the well-being of our staff through other rewards including merit pay, generous paid time off, a comprehensive health insurance plan, student loan repayment benefits, professional development training opportunities and up to $2,000 annual for education costs and fees relevant to Vera work, employer-funded retirement plan, and flexible time. To learn more about Vera’s benefits offerings, click here.

Application Process:

To receive further consideration for this career opportunity, applicants are asked preliminary questions about logistics, their interest and qualifications. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional details about their experience via a phone screen/form in advance of an invitation for a virtual or in-person interview with the team. Some searches may explore scenarios during the interview process and/or an assessment prior to reference checks and a hiring decision.

Vera Institute of Justice
34 35th St, Suite 4-2A, Brooklyn, NY 11232
Fax: (212) 941-9407
Please use only one method (online, mail or fax) of submission.
No phone calls, please. Only applicants selected for interviews will be contacted.

Vera is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without unlawful discrimination based on race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, military status, prior record of arrest or conviction, citizenship status, current employment status, or caregiver status.

Vera works to advance justice, particularly racial justice, in an increasingly multicultural country and globally connected world. We value diverse experiences, including with regard to educational background and justice system contact, and depend on a diverse staff to carry out our mission.

You'll use your healthcare administration experience to coordinate specialty care referrals that help military beneficiaries access timely medical services. Working alongside healthcare providers and administrative teams, you'll coordinate referral workflows, communicate with patients and specialty clinics, and help ensure referrals move efficiently from initiation through completion while supporting continuity of care.

Employment Type: PRN

Schedule: As needed; Monday-Friday | 7:30 AM-4:30 PM

Preferred

jobs.description:
This role comes with a $1,000 Sign-on bonus

The Medical Assistant reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Medical Assistant is a member of the health care team primarily responsible for providing support to physicians, nurses, and other licensed medical staff by facilitating efficient patient flow, assisting with various patient care activities, and performing related administrative functions. The Medical Assistant is responsible for ensuring efficient patient flow through the clinic; maintaining neat, clean and safe patient care areas; promoting patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner; safeguarding patient confidentiality.

Responsibilities:

• Assures efficient patient flow through the site: Escorts patient to exam room, identifies patient with 2 identifiers and prepares patient for examination. Obtains accurate vital signs, per organization standards. Documents reason for visit and updates/confirms, allergies, smoking history and pharmacy information. Promptly informs the provider and registered nurse of any significant change in vital signs or acute symptoms. Anticipates/sets up equipment or supplies needed for visit. Cleans and prepares exam room for next patient. Responds to needs to expedite visits and maintain flow of patients and prioritize tasks accordingly.

• Assists practitioner with medical and surgical procedures in accordance with established protocols such as: Electrocardiogram (ECG), venipuncture, immunizations, setting up procedure trays, specimen collection and/or Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) waived testing as directed by Provider.

• Provides high quality care by: Prepares and stocks all exam rooms in treatment area by following established protocols for disinfecting and sterilizing equipment and instruments. Participates in environmental safety rounds. Maintains vaccine/medication inventory. Monitors and maintains equipment and instruments according to clinic guidelines. Assists in ordering supplies and correctly disposes of all expired items. Adheres to office opening and closing procedures.

• Functions as an integral part of the patient care team and promotes patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner: Accepts and performs delegated responsibilities in a positive manner. Offers assistance to others. Attends and participates in staff meetings. Communicates appropriately and effectively with patients and patient care team (in the office and on the phone)

• Performs delegated procedures common to the specialty area in a safe, effective, and efficient manner (see specialty practice addendum)

• Performs all other duties as assigned by the Supervisor or Manager

Required:

• High school diploma or GED.
• Current certification in one of the below or must have written proof of meeting candidate eligibility requirements for writing one of the five eligible certification exams (AAMA, AMT, NCCT, NHA, NRCMA)Accepted documentation:New MA Graduates within six (6) months from date of graduation from an MA Program must submit: a letter from the school or a letter from the certifying bodyNon-Certified MAs or new graduates past six (6) months from date of graduation from an MA program must submit: a letter from the certifying bodyWithin first six months of employment, will complete one of the following certifications after up to two test attempts:Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) through American Association of Medical Assistants (AAMA)Registered Medical Assistant (RMA) through American Medical Technologists (AMT) orNational Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA) through the National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT)Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA) through the National Healthcareer Association (NHA)Nationally Registered Certified Medical Assistant (NRCMA) through the National Association for Health Professionals (NAHP)Signed acknowledgement during onboarding that certification must be attained within six (6) months, as a condition of employment
• American Heart Association accredited Basic Life Support (BLS/CPR) certification.
• Zero (0) to two (2) years’ experience in a relevant role.
• Strong computer skills.

Preferred:

• Completion of accredited Medical Assistant training program.
• One to two years of ambulatory care experience.
• Experience with electronic medical record.

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

jobs.title: 2026-2027 Lower Elementary School Leave Replacement Drama Teacher
jobs.description:
Lower Elementary School Leave Replacement Drama Teacher

(2026 - 2027 School Year)

Coney Island Preparatory Public Charter School

Brooklyn, New York

What is the Role?

Join us in welcoming our youngest scholars and their families into education and carve out their pathway to success in Kindergarten through second grade and beyond. As an educator of early learners you’re passionate about providing consistency and building young minds. Electives at Coney Island Prep bring creativity to the learning process and enrich academic experiences. As a Leave Replacement Drama Teacher, you bring fun and joy to school on a daily basis and are committed to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment that encourages creativity, self-expression, as well as critical thinking.

The Leave Replacement Drama Teacher will be hired by the Principal. Continued employment beyond the leave replacement term is contingent on performance and vacancies within and across the organization. In some cases employment opportunities may be at another Coney Island Prep campus in grades 3 - 12.

What You’ll Be Asked To Do

• Create standards-aligned curriculum and content

• On a daily basis, teach academically rigorous and culturally relevant lesson plans, materials, and assessments, and differentiate as needed

• Communicate effectively with all scholars, their families, and staff

• Commit to a culture of consistently implementing school-wide systems, structures, and procedures

• Eradicate the effects of racism, poverty and other forms of oppression in our school community by making resources, opportunities, support systems, and classrooms equitable and accessible for all our stakeholders

• Analyze and action plan using instructional and culture data to improve teaching practice and strengthen student outcomes

• Be proactive in creating a positive, structured, results-oriented and fun learning environment that supports the needs of students with various abilities and experiences

• Participate in school community responsibilities such as lunch duty, dismissal and hallway duties, daily homeroom, weekly content and grade team meetings, whole-staff professional development, lesson internalization and practice

What You’ll Need

• Passion for education and a dedication to Coney Island Prep’s mission, beliefs, and values and its commitment to anti-racism

• Steadfast belief that all students can achieve at the highest academic levels and deserve an opportunity to succeed in the college and career of their choice

• Bachelor's degree and NYS teaching certification required, Master’s degree strongly preferred; we offer $2,000 towards the completion of a Master’s degree and NY State certification within two years of employment

• Cultural competencies to work in low-income communities and a willingness to examine your beliefs and biases across lines of difference

• Proven organizational, oral, and written communication skills; timeliness; accuracy; consistent and regular communication; and ability to meet deadlines

• Culturally responsive and age-appropriate conflict resolution skills

• Self-reflective and open to feedback, with the ambition and desire to grow and develop

• A positive, solution-oriented attitude and drive for excellence

• Eagerness to work collaboratively as part of a team

• A strong track record of building positive relationships with families, students and staff, while demonstrating value towards diversity and inclusivity

Who are we?

Coney Island Prep Lower Elementary School blends joy, rigor, and high expectations to ensure our 320 scholars in K-2 are ready to succeed. With two teachers in every classroom, smaller teacher to student ratios help accelerate learning and allow for tailored instruction for each scholar. We leverage a research-backed approach to teach the science of reading and focus heavily on phonics instruction, word recognition, vocabulary, background knowledge and comprehension skills, to cultivate our young learners’ strong reading abilities from the moment they step into our building.

Commitment to Anti-racism, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Justice

Coney Island Prep is committed to building a team that collectively reflects the various backgrounds, experiences, and identities of our scholars. We recognize and respond to different points of access, so that everyone maximizes their highest potential. We also recognize that because of institutionalized racism and systemic oppression, historically marginalized groups are at a disadvantage when it comes to most application and hiring processes. We want to ensure that all candidates, regardless of their identity, are able to demonstrate their qualifications and are not limited by a lack of opportunity or access. We are committed to creating a space where everyone’s identity is acknowledged, respected, and welcomed. We are intentional about creating an environment where people feel comfortable being their authentic selves at work by constantly examining our organization culture and challenging our traditions.

Benefits and Compensation

jobs.title: Industrial Lube Technician (Night Shift)
jobs.description:
Harsco Environmental is seeking a safety-focused and reliable Lube Technician to support the maintenance and performance of heavy mobile equipment operating in industrial and steel mill environments. The Lube Technician is responsible for performing preventive maintenance services including lubrication, fluid changes, filter replacements, inspections, and basic mechanical support on equipment such as loaders, excavators, material handlers, haul trucks, skid steers, forklifts, and overhead cranes. This position plays a critical role in maximizing equipment uptime, reducing breakdowns, and supporting safe operations.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Perform scheduled preventive maintenance services on heavy equipment according to manufacturer and company standards.
• Change engine oil, hydraulic oil, transmission fluid, gear oil, coolant, and other operating fluids.
• Inspect, lubricate, and service grease points on mobile equipment and designated plant equipment.
• Replace fuel, oil, air, hydraulic, and coolant filters.
• Conduct equipment inspections and identify potential mechanical issues, leaks, excessive wear, or safety concerns.
• Check and maintain proper fluid levels in engines, transmissions, differentials, hydraulic systems, and cooling systems.
• Service and assist with preventive maintenance activities on overhead cranes and other industrial material handling equipment as required.
• Document maintenance activities, inspections, and service records accurately.
• Notify supervisors and mechanics of equipment deficiencies requiring repair.
• Maintain clean and organized work areas, service trucks, tools, and maintenance facilities.
• Follow all Harsco Environmental safety policies, lockout/tagout procedures, and site-specific requirements.
• Support mechanics with general repair work when needed.
• Participate in safety meetings, training programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED preferred.
• Previous experience performing lubrication and preventive maintenance on heavy equipment, mining equipment, construction equipment, or industrial machinery preferred.
• Basic mechanical aptitude and understanding of diesel-powered equipment.
• Ability to identify fluid leaks, worn components, and abnormal equipment conditions.
• Ability to safely operate service trucks and lubrication equipment.
• Valid driver's license required.
• Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions and industrial environments.
• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and perform physical labor including climbing, kneeling, bending, and standing for extended periods.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience working in steel mills, manufacturing facilities, mining operations, or heavy industrial environments.
• Knowledge of Caterpillar, Komatsu, Volvo, John Deere, Sennebogen, Terex, or similar heavy equipment.
• Familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS).
• OSHA, MSHA, or industrial safety training experience.

Working Conditions

• Work is performed in active industrial and steel manufacturing environments.
• Exposure to heat, dust, noise, vibration, moving equipment, and outdoor weather conditions.
• Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, and steel-toed boots.
• May require overtime, weekends, holidays, and rotating shifts based on operational needs.

Additional Information

We offer competitive benefits, including health insurance, life insurance and disability plans, as well as a 401k with company matching.
