jobs.title: Field Sales Representative - Stoke-On-Trent
jobs.description:
Field Sales Representative

Location: Stoke-on-Trent, covering Stoke-on-Trent or surrounding areas (fully field-based)

£50,000–£90,000 OTE (£30,000–£54,000 base salary + uncapped commission, based on experience) + £800 monthly car allowance and a comprehensive benefits package

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re ambitious, enjoy meeting new people and want to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

We’re looking for ambitious, driven people to join our growing Field Sales team and help bring Teya to more local businesses across the UK.

As a Field Sales Representative, you’ll take ownership of your own territory, getting out into your local community, meeting business owners face-to-face and showing them how Teya can help their businesses thrive.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the field, building relationships and winning new business. You’ll have the freedom to manage your territory, the support of a team that wants you to succeed, and the opportunity to build a rewarding career in sales.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Own your territory: Proactively identify and engage local businesses through face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals and other opportunities to generate new business.

 - Build meaningful relationships: Get to know business owners, understand their challenges and identify how Teya’s products and services can make their lives easier.

 - Win new Members: Use a consultative, value-led approach to demonstrate Teya’s solutions, build trust and turn conversations into long-term customer relationships.

 - Deliver results: Take ownership of your sales performance, maintain a healthy pipeline and consistently work towards your commercial targets.

 - See things through: Take responsibility for your Members’ experience from the first conversation through to onboarding, ensuring they’re set up successfully and ready to start using Teya.

 - Keep learning: Develop strong knowledge of our products, competitors and sales methodology through structured training, coaching and feedback.

 - Represent Teya: Be a trusted face of Teya in your local community, delivering the genuine care and hospitality that we want every Member to experience.

 - Help us improve: Share insights from the field to help us continuously improve our products, sales approach and Member experience.

Your Story

We believe great salespeople come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might already be an experienced field sales professional with a strong track record of winning new business. Or you might be earlier in your career, with the ambition, drive and potential to become an exceptional salesperson.

What matters most to us is your mindset, your ability to connect with people and your willingness to learn and improve.

We’re looking for people who bring:

 - Ambition and drive: You’re motivated to succeed, enjoy working towards challenging goals and take pride in delivering great results.

 - A competitive mindset: You enjoy winning, hold yourself to high standards and are always looking for ways to improve.

 - Resilience and determination: You’re comfortable with rejection, stay positive when things get tough and don’t give up easily.

 - Strong people skills: You enjoy meeting new people, build rapport naturally and can have meaningful conversations with business owners from all walks of life.

 - Curiosity and commercial awareness: You ask good questions, listen carefully and want to understand what makes a business successful.

 - Coachability: You’re open to feedback, willing to challenge yourself and committed to developing your skills.

 - Ownership and self-discipline: You’re organised, proactive and comfortable managing your own time and priorities in a field-based role.

 - A genuine care for others: You understand that great sales isn’t just about closing a deal. It’s about doing what’s right for the customer and building trust that lasts.

Experience in field sales, business development, payments or financial services is an advantage, but not essential for every level. We care just as much about your potential as your experience.

You’ll also need:

 - Fluency in English.

 - A full UK driving licence and access to a car.

 - The right to work in the UK.

 - Willingness to work in a fully field-based role, travelling regularly throughout your territory.

The Perks

We believe great performance should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

 - £30,000–£54,000 base salary, depending on your experience and demonstrated capability.

 - Uncapped commission.

 - £800 per month car allowance (£9,600 annually), on top of your salary and commission.

 - 25 days of paid annual leave, plus UK bank holidays.

 - Bupa private healthcare and life insurance.

 - Employer pension contributions through our company pension scheme.

 - Free gym membership through Wellhub, alongside one-to-one therapy sessions, meditation and digital fitness and nutrition apps.

 - Structured onboarding, practical sales training, ongoing coaching and opportunities to grow your career at Teya.

What Happens Next?

Our recruitment process is designed to help us get to know you, understand your strengths and give you a genuine opportunity to show us what you can do.

Stage 1 - Introductory conversation (30 minutes) 
 A conversation with our Talent team to learn more about you, your motivation and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2 - Hiring Manager Interview (60 minutes) 
 An opportunity to explore your experience, how you approach challenges and what makes you successful.

Stage 3 - Final Assessment (60 minutes) 
 You’ll meet members of our Sales leadership team, present a short territory plan and take part in a practical sales role-play. We’ll share everything you need to prepare in advance.

We know interviews are a two-way process, and we’ll make sure you have plenty of opportunities to ask questions and get to know us along the way.

Teya is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, including those without a traditional sales or commercial track record.

Teya is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or background can thrive and do their best work. We believe that a diverse team leads to better ideas, stronger outcomes, and a more supportive workplace for all.

If you require any reasonable adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process whether for interviews, assessments, or other parts of the application—we encourage you to let us know. We are committed to ensuring that every candidate has a fair and accessible experience with us.

jobs.title: Meewerkstage Talent Management
jobs.description:
Start in Februari 2027 als Talent Management stagiair(e) bij ons op kantoor in Utrecht en Amsterdam. Tijdens deze stage draag je bij aan het versterken van de leer- en ontwikkel cultuur binnen het Noord-Europa cluster en ondersteun je het team bij uiteenlopende Talent Management activiteiten, zoals onze jaarlijkse performance cycle, onboarding, learning & development en employee engagement.

Wat je zoal gaat doen:

• Je ondersteunt bij de ontwikkeling en uitvoering van initiatieven op het gebied van Learning & Development, Performance Management, Talent Management en Employee Engagement.
• Je draagt actief bij aan de organisatie en communicatie van trainingen, workshops en andere leeractiviteiten voor medewerkers binnen Noord-Europa.
• Je coördineert onderdelen van het onboardingprogramma voor nieuwe medewerkers en zorgt er zo voor dat nieuwe collega’s een vliegende start maken.
• Je beheert de mailbox van het Talent Management Team en zorgt voor een soepele opvolging van vragen en verzoeken.
• Je werkt samen met verschillende stakeholders binnen HR en de business en krijgt inzicht in een breed scala aan talent- en ontwikkelvraagstukken.

Bij JDE Peet’s krijg je de kans om écht het verschil te maken. Je werkt hands-on en kunt je stempel drukken, terwijl je samenwerkt met een team dat gedreven is door één gemeenschappelijk doel. Wij zijn een energiek en snelgroeiend bedrijf, gericht op wat echt belangrijk is. Hier telt lef: het lef om nieuwe ideeën te proberen, om buiten de gebaande paden te denken en om impact te maken.

Ben jij nieuwsgierig, leergierig en vol ideeën? Dan willen we jou graag leren kennen!

• Studie: Je staat ingeschreven bij een HBO of WO-opleiding (BSc. of MSc.) gedurende je hele stage periode, bij voorkeur in HR, Psychologie, Sociologie, Bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare studie.
• Skills: Je bent handig met MS Office (met name PowerPoint, Excel en Outlook) en communiceert vloeiend in zowel Nederlands als Engels.
• Persoonlijkheid: Je bent nieuwsgierig, proactief en leergierig. Je werkt gestructureerd, neemt initiatief en schakelt gemakkelijk met verschillende stakeholders. Zowel zelfstandig werken als samenwerken in een team gaat je goed af.
• Toewijding: Je bent beschikbaar van februari tot en met juli 2027, met de mogelijkheid om je stage te verlengen tot augustus. Dit betreft een meewerkstage waarin je praktijkervaring opdoet en actief onderdeel wordt van het team.
• Beschikbaarheid: Je bent beschikbaar voor 4 of 5 dagen per week. Je werkt voornamelijk vanuit onze kantoren in Utrecht en Amsterdam, met de mogelijkheid om één dag per week vanuit huis te werken.

Werken bij JDE Peet’s betekent impact maken in een dynamische en ambitieuze omgeving. Je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s, viert successen en krijgt volop kansen om je verder te ontwikkelen. Iedereen is erop gericht om te doen wat juist is – overal ter wereld. Wat je hier doet, wordt opgemerkt.

Wat levert het jou op?

• Een maandelijkse stagevergoeding van €525 (fulltime)
• Reiskostenvergoeding als je geen gratis (studenten) OV hebt
• Betaalde vakantiedagen gedurende je stageperiode

Ben je klaar om jouw mogelijkheden binnen JDE Peet's te ontdekken? We zijn benieuwd of je liever koffie of thee hebt tijdens je sollicitatiegesprek! 😉

Dit is hoe je kunt solliciteren:

• Upload je cv.

• Na je sollicitatie nemen we binnen drie weken contact met je op om je te laten weten wat de volgende stappen zijn.

• Tijdens het sollicitatieproces word je gevraagd om een online assessment te doen en minimaal één interview op ons kantoor in Utrecht of Amsterdam.

Als je vragen hebt, aarzel dan niet om contact op te nemen met onze Talent Acquisition stagiair Dounia Addouti via dounia.addouti@jdecoffee.com - We zijn er om te helpen!

Wij geloven dat koffie mensen verbindt en kansen creëert. Als één team werken we dagelijks aan impact, geleid door onze waarden: Dare to Amaze, Own It, Make It Simple en Win Together. Je krijgt hier ruimte om te innoveren, te groeien en samen successen te behalen in een internationale omgeving.

Bij JDE Peet’s streven we naar een betere toekomst, waarin we iedereen op een authentieke manier bedienen, weerspiegelen en omarmen. Wij geloven in het bevorderen van een meer diverse, eerlijke en inclusieve organisatie, waar iedereen zich comfortabel voelt om echt zichzelf te zijn en zijn of haar volledige potentieel kan benutten. Dit betekent dat we geen enkele vorm van discriminatie tolereren op basis van ras, etniciteit, geslacht, genderidentiteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie, nationaliteit, leeftijd, beperking of enig ander door de wet beschermd kenmerk.

Tijdens de hele loopbaan van onze medewerkers staat diversiteit, gelijkheid en inclusie (DE&I) centraal in onze personeelsprocessen. Dit stelt ons in staat objectiviteit te waarborgen en mogelijke vooroordelen te elimineren, zodat iedereen een inclusieve ervaring op de werkvloer heeft. Aarzel niet om contact op te nemen als je aanpassingen nodig hebt tijdens het wervingsproces.

Onze inspanningen op dit gebied hebben ons de prestigieuze Catalyst Award opgeleverd, evenals de Fair Pay Leader-certificering in 2025, dankzij een onverklaarde loonkloof tussen mannen en vrouwen van slechts 0,52%.

Een online assessment maakt onderdeel uit van de procedure.

JDE Peet’s - now part of Keurig Dr Pepper – is the world’s leading pure-play coffee company, with a presence in more than 100 markets. Guided by our ‘Reignite the Amazing’ strategy, we are focused on brand-led growth across three big bets: Peet’s, L’OR, and our 10 strategically selected local icons led by Jacobs.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
The Enterprise Account Executive will generate new business sales revenue in the West region. This will be achieved through account planning, territory planning, working with Nexthink partners, business development techniques, and field-based sales activities. The ideal candidate will have:

Why this role matters

The next evolution of IT is not just about uptime. It is about experience, productivity, automation, and measurable business value.

As an Enterprise Account Executive at Nexthink, you will help CIOs, Digital Workplace leaders, End User Computing teams, Service Desk leaders, and IT Operations executives answer questions like:

• How do we find and fix technology issues before employees report them?
• How do we reduce ticket volume and improve service quality at scale?
• How do we measure whether employees are actually adopting new tools, including AI?
• How do we turn IT from a cost center into a driver of productivity and employee experience?
• How do we make digital work feel seamless?

You help customers rethink the operating model of enterprise IT.

What you will do

You will own new business growth across your assigned territory by building a strategic territory plan, creating executive-level demand, and driving complex enterprise sales cycles from initial engagement through close.

• Build, manage, and execute a regional sales strategy for the North Central territory.
• Prospect aggressively into enterprise accounts and develop qualified pipeline.
• Identify business pains tied to employee productivity, IT support, application adoption, digital transformation, and AI readiness.
• Engage multiple stakeholders across IT, Digital Workplace, End User Computing, Service Management, Infrastructure, Security, Procurement, and executive leadership.
• Evangelize Nexthink’s value proposition and educate customers on the rapidly evolving DEX category.
• Partner with Nexthink’s business development, marketing, channel, solution consulting, and professional services teams to create and advance opportunities.
• Lead discovery, business case development, executive presentations, proof-of-concept alignment, negotiation, and close.
• Manage customer expectations throughout evaluations and proof-of-concept cycles.
• Sell the full Nexthink solution, including software, services, and support, to ensure long-term customer success.
• Build trusted relationships that create expansion opportunities and durable customer value.
• Consistently exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual bookings targets.

#LI-Remote

What makes you a strong fit

You are a high-performing enterprise seller who knows how to create a market, not just respond to one. You are energized by new categories, complex problems, and executive conversations where you can connect technology to measurable business outcomes.

• 7+ years of enterprise technology sales experience in a fast-paced, competitive B2B SaaS or enterprise software environment.
• A proven record of quota overachievement, such as President’s Club, top rep performance, or consistent attainment above plan.
• Experience selling complex solutions to large enterprise IT organizations.
• Ability to evangelize emerging categories and educate buyers on new ways of solving business problems.
• Strong executive presence and the ability to sell across technical, operational, and business stakeholders.
• Discipline in territory planning, account strategy, pipeline generation, qualification, forecasting, and deal execution.
• Comfort managing proof-of-concept processes and aligning technical validation to business value.
• A consultative sales approach with strong discovery, storytelling, and value-selling skills.
• High ownership, urgency, resilience, and intellectual curiosity.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
• Sold disruptive or category-creating technology in an early-stage, high-growth, or market-expansion environment.
• A track record of opening new logos and building territory from the ground up.
• The ability to simplify complex technical concepts into clear business outcomes.
• A strong partner ecosystem mindset and experience working with channel, alliance, or services partners.
• The confidence to challenge customer assumptions while building trust.

The base salary for this role is $150,000-180,000 gross per year, with a total on-target earnings (OTE) range of $300,000-360,000 with additional opportunity to earn commissions above this range.

We are the pioneers and trailblazers of a global IT Market Category (DEX) that is shaping the future of how the world works, giving our customers’ IT Teams total digital visibility across their enterprise. Our innovative solutions integrate real-time analytics, automation, and employee feedback across all endpoints. This enables our IT teams to solve complex technical challenges, create ever more productive workplaces, and deliver happy, satisfied employees in the digital workplace.

With over 1200 employees across 5 continents, Nexthink operates as One Team, connecting, collaborating and innovating to continuously grow. We call our employees ‘Nexthinkers’ and our commitment to diversity, inclusion, and equity is second to none. We currently have over 75 nationalities working with us, from all cultures and backgrounds, speaking many different languages

Total Rewards @ Nexthink

At Nexthink, we offer one of the most comprehensive and generous benefits plans.  Your total rewards compensation package includes base salary and may also include a commission or performance bonus plan.  We provide our US employees with 100% covered company benefits that consist of health, dental, vision as well as access to life insurance, long-term disability, and accidental death/personal loss coverage.

In addition, we offer:

• 🏖️ Flexible Hours and unlimited vacation (employees have unlimited paid time off on top of the 15 days of holidays we offer), 11 company-paid holidays, and 3 extra days for volunteering.
• 🏡 Hybrid work model that balances office and remote work, with structured onboarding to foster connections and team integration.
• 📚 Free access to professional training platforms to explore your interests and enhance your skills.
• 🍼 Up to 16 weeks of paid leave for birthing parents/primary caregivers, 6 weeks for secondary caregivers.
• 💰 Plan for the future with a 401(k) plan featuring up to 4% company matching contributions, vesting immediately, to grow your retirement savings.
• 📣 Bonuses for referring successful hires after three months of continuous employment.

Base salary ranges are determined by country, role, level, experience, and skills. The range displayed on each job posting reflects Nexthink’s good faith determination of the minimum and maximum targets for new hire salaries across all US locations. Individual pay is determined by related factors, including job skills, experience, and relevant education or training, which may impact a final offer. Your Talent Acquisition Partner can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Senior Talent Partner & Advisor (Product)
jobs.description:
About OpenFx

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, Paypal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We're backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NfX and other top-tier investors.

The role:

We are hiring a senior talent partner and advisor, dedicated to hiring for the Product team. The product team includes product management, product design, product operations, product analytics and adjacent roles. Many of these are senior, specialised searches for people who have shipped payments, fintech or infrastructure products in a regulated industry, spanning the US, India, UK / Europe and the Middle East. You own every product search end to end, from intake with the hiring manager to a signed offer, in whichever geography the role sits. This is a hands-on sourcing and closing role, not a generalist or people ops role.

What you will do:

• Own the full hiring lifecycle for all product roles across geographies: intake, sourcing, screening, interview coordination, feedback loops, offer negotiation and close

• Run outbound-led sourcing for product talent (LinkedIn, referrals, product and fintech communities), with the ability to find strong product builders who are not actively looking

• Partner closely with product leaders to define role requirements, calibrate on profiles and hold a high bar on senior hires

• Navigate the differences in hiring across markets: talent pools, compensation norms, notice periods, visa and relocation considerations

• Run a tight, well-communicated candidate experience and keep hiring managers accountable to interview timelines

• Keep Greenhouse (and any ATS in use) clean and current for your roles: pipelines, scorecards, stage data

• Manage agencies on product searches where used, and keep agency spend under control

• Report weekly on pipeline health, pass-through rates and time to hire for product roles

What we are looking for (Must Haves):

• 10 to 12 years in talent acquisition, with at least 6 years recruiting product roles at a high-growth startup or scale-up

• Proven track record of closing senior and specialised product hires (PMs, product designers, product leads) through outbound sourcing, not agency hand-offs

• Experience hiring in the US plus at least one of our other core regions: India, UK / Europe or UAE / Middle East

• Can assess product talent credibly: understands what strong product managers and designers in payments, fintech or infrastructure look like and can screen for it

• Comfortable with Greenhouse or a comparable ATS

• Clear, direct communicator who is comfortable engaging with the hiring managers and managing senior stakeholders

What we are looking for (Good to have):

• Fintech, payments or crypto background

• Experience hiring product talent for B2B or infrastructure products in a regulated industry

• Agency management experience

• Prior in-house experience at a Series A or B company

What we offer

Competitive salary and benefits, equity, and a fast-moving fintech environment where your hires shape what the company builds.

OpenFX is an equal opportunity employer.

We are an In-Office Company and hence expect our colleagues to collaborate and innovate while being present in the Office

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
Joining Collibra’s AI Product Management team

Collibra’s AI Product Management team sets how we build AI into our platform and how we help customers govern and trust their own AI systems. You will work with the Director of AI Engineering to shape our AI strategy and roadmap, and with Product and Engineering leaders to ship AI features customers use. You will report directly to the Vice President, Product Management. This role is needed now because AI is central to Collibra’s strategy, and you will help define what responsible, enterprise-grade AI looks like in data governance.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York office. Our hybrid model means you’ll work from the office at least two days each week. This setup helps us stay connected, work more closely together, and keep making progress as a team.

Staff Product Managers, AI at Collibra are responsible for

• Defining Collibra’s AI product strategy and 12-month roadmap with the Director of AI Engineering and Product and Engineering leaders, so AI investments stay focused on where customers and the market are heading.

• Co-authoring customer-facing AI features from problem framing through launch and adoption, working directly with customers on challenges such as data management restrictions and custom AI models, so features solve real problems and get used.

• Leading evaluation of AI models and approaches with Engineering, for both internal use and the customer platform (central model evaluation, platform AI testing, emerging AI paradigms), so Collibra builds on the most capable and appropriate foundation.

• Setting responsible AI standards with Engineering, Legal, and Security, including a pre-launch review for AI features, so what we ship meets our standards for quality, transparency, and compliance.

You have

• 5+ years of product management experience.

• Experience working on AI or ML-powered software, including taking an AI or ML feature from design to launch with engineers.

• Experience presenting product strategy to senior or executive leadership.

jobs.title: Energy Storage System (ESS) Intern (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT's Energy Storage System team is working on one of the most foundational questions behind our Seagliders: how do we store and deliver the energy that gets them across the water, safely and efficiently, mission after mission. As our ESS Intern, you'll dig directly into that question — splitting your time between hands-on test support, battery characterization, and simulation work that spans our Squire and Viceroy programs. You'll help the team understand how individual cells and full packs actually behave under real conditions, how they should be integrated into our platforms, and how to optimally design the high voltage vehicle architecture. This isn't a narrow, single-task internship — it's a genuinely broad technical role with real scope behind it, built for someone who wants to learn by doing.

You'll sit within our Hardware Engineering group, working closely with the Electrical Systems and Mechanical teams, where precision and curiosity go hand in hand. The team moves fast and expects you to pick up REGENT-specific tools and architectures quickly, but once you're oriented, you'll be trusted to run with real analysis and contribute findings that shape how we think about battery integration going forward. 

If you're a student with strong engineering fundamentals who gets energized by ambiguity, hands-on testing, and the chance to help define how next-generation electric watercraft get their power, this is a place where you'll do work that matters from day one.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Characterize Battery Packs: You'll run tests on battery packs to understand how they perform under the conditions our Seagliders actually face. Your findings will directly inform how the team evaluates viable energy storage options.

 - Support Paladin Test Operations: You'll get hands-on with test support and battery servicing, working alongside engineers who rely on accurate, well-documented testing to move programs forward. This is where you'll build real intuition for how packs behave outside of a datasheet.

 - Model Mission-Profile Performance: Using Python or MATLAB, you'll build simulations that show how battery performance holds up across different mission profiles. This work helps the team make informed tradeoffs long before hardware decisions are finalized.

 - Contribute to Integration Documentation: You'll help document how battery systems integrate into REGENT's high voltage architecture across platforms. Clear, thorough documentation here keeps the whole team moving faster.

 - Own Energy Budgets and Trade Studies: You'll build and refine energy budgets and trade studies in Excel that compare options across cost, performance, and integration complexity. These studies feed directly into engineering decisions on the program.

 - Track Cell and Pack Data: You'll help monitor pack-specific characteristics during testing, keeping an eye on the details that matter for performance and safety. Good data here is the foundation for everything else the team builds on top of it.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Strong Engineering Fundamentals: You're currently a senior or graduate student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or chemical engineering. You come in with the core fundamentals already in place, ready to apply them from week one.

 - Li-ion Battery Knowledge: You understand the basics of lithium-ion systems — capacity, C-rate, state of charge, internal resistance, voltage curves, and series/parallel configurations. This foundation is essential to the work you'll be doing all summer.

 - Analytical Toolkit: You're proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis and modeling, and you're comfortable building energy budgets and trade studies in Excel. A significant part of this role involves analyzing battery performance across different mission profiles.

 - Comfort With Ambiguity: You're self-directed and don't need every task spelled out to make meaningful progress. You can take a loosely defined problem and figure out how to move it forward.

 - Clear Communication: You can explain your findings and tradeoffs to engineers in a way that's useful and easy to act on. Translating technical analysis into clear takeaways is a core part of this role.

 - CAD Familiarity, A Plus: Experience with a 3D CAD tool like SolidWorks, Fusion, or Creo, along with the ability to produce clear drawings, would help you move quickly and bridge gaps between electrical and mechanical work.

 - Pack and Simulation Experience, A Plus: Any exposure to pack-level design work — cell selection, BMS architecture, busbars, thermal management — or to battery simulation tools like PyBaMM, Simulink/Simscape Battery, or COMSOL will help you hit the ground running.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

• Be a taste maker and demonstrate good judgement in your domain.

• Regularly meet and engage with our most strategic customers to bring the customer voice alongside product data into product decisions.

• Leverage AI tools through every step of the process, defining new ways of working and democratizing design at Samsara.

• Stay well informed on the emerging trends, tools, and technology. Give back to the community.

• Ship code to production across our design system, web products, and mobile apps.

• Set the bar for what great looks like through building and shipping.

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 10+ years of product design experience designing UX/UI for web and mobile applications, with a track record of leading work that spans multiple product areas.

• A strong portfolio and/or case studies showing design craft and quantified impact at the level of multiple product areas or platform-wide systems, not just a single feature. We cannot consider applications without a portfolio at this time.

• Deep interaction and visual design skills, with the judgment to define new patterns other designers and teams build on.

• Experience mentoring designers formally and informally.

Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary

$143,640—$256,500 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. Belonging at Samsara

jobs.title: Space Operations Subject Matter Expert (SME)
jobs.description:
This is a U.S. based position. All of the programs we support require U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. All work must be conducted within the continental U.S.

Who we are:

Raft (https://TeamRaft.com) is a customer-obsessed non-traditional defense tech company dedicated to empowering U.S. military and government agencies with cutting-edge AI/ML and data solutions. We are a leader in autonomous data fusion and Agentic AI, with a purposeful focus on Distributed Data Systems, Platforms at Scale, and Complex Application Development. With headquarters in McLean, VA, our range of clients includes innovative federal and public agencies leveraging design thinking, cutting-edge tech stack, and cloud-native ecosystem. We build digital solutions that impact the lives of millions of Americans.

About the role:

Raft is seeking a Space Operations Subject Matter Expert (SME) with firsthand experience conducting military space operations. We are looking for someone who understands the operational environment, the challenges facing Guardians, and the capabilities needed to execute space missions effectively.

This role is ideal for a former space operator who wants to continue contributing to the mission by working directly with operational units and engineering teams to develop and deliver mission-focused software capabilities.

What You'll Do

• Serve as a space operations SME, bringing firsthand operational knowledge to Raft's engineering and product teams.

• Engage directly with Space Force operators and mission stakeholders to understand operational challenges, workflows, and capability gaps.

• Translate operational requirements into actionable software and technology capabilities.

• Support the development and integration of solutions for Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Space Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and other space mission areas.

• Provide operational insight during product design, development, demonstrations, and exercises.

• Build and maintain relationships across Space Force mission organizations and operational units.

• Help ensure Raft's products align with real-world mission needs and operational priorities.

Required Qualifications

• Prior military experience as a space operator, preferably within the U.S. Space Force or U.S. Air Force.

• Strong understanding of military space operations, operational planning, and mission execution.

• Experience working within space operations squadrons, mission crews, or operational command organizations.

• Ability to communicate effectively with both military operators and technical engineering teams.

• Strong understanding of the operational challenges associated with modern space missions.

• Must currently reside in Colorado Springs, CO, or be willing to relocate.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Highly Preferred

• Operational experience supporting Mission Delta 2, Mission Delta 7, or other U.S. Space Force Mission Deltas.

• Hands-on experience with operational applications, tools, and systems used by Space Force operators, including an understanding of their workflows, capabilities, and limitations.

• Experience with space battle management, space command and control (C2), space surveillance, or space domain awareness.

• Familiarity with Space Force operational systems, data sources, and mission workflows.

• Experience participating in operational exercises, mission planning, or capability development.

• Existing relationships within the Colorado Springs Space Force operational community..

Clearance Requirements:

• Active Secret or Top Secret/SCI clearance

Salary Range: $200,000.00 - $300,000.00

Work Type:

• Onsite in Colorado Springs, CO

Why Raft

At Raft, you'll work alongside engineers and mission experts developing software capabilities for some of the Department of Defense's most important operational challenges. We value people who have operated these systems, understand their limitations, and have a clear perspective on what needs to improve. This is an opportunity to take your operational experience beyond the mission floor and directly influence the products that support the next generation of space operations

What we will offer you:

• Highly competitive salary

• Fully covered healthcare, dental, and vision coverage

• 401(k) and company match

• Take as you need PTO + 11 paid holidays

• Education & training benefits

• Generous Referral Bonuses

• And More!

Our Vision Statement:

We bridge the gap between humans and data through radical transparency and our obsession with the mission.

Our Customer Obsession:

We will approach every deliverable like it's a product. We will adopt a customer-obsessed mentality. As we grow, and our footprint becomes larger, teams and employees will treat each other not only as teammates but customers. We must live the customer-obsessed mindset, always. This will help us scale and it will translate to the interactions that our Rafters have with their clients and other product teams that they integrate with. Our culture will enable our success and set us apart from other companies.

How do we get there?

Public-sector modernization is critical for us to live in a better world. We, at Raft, want to innovate and solve complex problems. And, if we are successful, our generation and the ones that follow us will live in a delightful, efficient, and accessible world where out-of-box thinking, and collaboration is a norm.

Raft’s core philosophy is Ubuntu: I Am, Because We are. We support our “nadi” by elevating the other Rafters. We work as a hyper collaborative team where each team member brings a unique perspective, adding value that did not exist before. People make Raft special. We celebrate each other and our cognitive and cultural diversity. We are devoted to our practice of innovation and collaboration.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

Job Title: Adult Acute Speech and Language Therapist

Banding: Band 6 / 7

Location: Scunthorpe General Hospital

Start Date: ASAP

Duration: Ongoing Contract

Hourly Rate: TBC depending on experience

Working Hours: Full-time or Part-time Considered

Job Overview

Pulse is currently seeking an experienced Adult Acute Speech and Language Therapist to join the team at Scunthorpe General Hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to work across acute wards and specialist stroke services, supporting adults with acquired communication and swallowing difficulties. The successful candidate will provide highly specialist assessment and intervention, working closely with multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care.

The role also offers opportunities to support outpatient clinics and community caseloads through home visits, alongside involvement in specialist instrumental swallowing assessment services, including Videofluoroscopy (VFSS) and FEES.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide specialist assessment and treatment for adults with acquired communication and swallowing disorders.

• Manage patients across acute wards and stroke rehabilitation services.

• Assess, diagnose, and treat dysphagia using evidence-based approaches.

• Support the delivery of Videofluoroscopy (VFSS) clinics and inpatient FEES services.

• Provide outpatient support and home visits for community patients where appropriate.

• Triage and prioritize referrals and caseloads effectively within a busy clinical environment.

• Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to optimize patient outcomes.

• Support, supervise, and provide guidance to junior members of the Speech and Language Therapy team.

• Maintain accurate and timely clinical records in line with professional standards.

• Contribute to service development, audits, and quality improvement initiatives.

Qualifications and Experience

• Degree or equivalent qualification in Speech and Language Therapy.

• HCPC registration.

• Experience working within adult acute Speech and Language Therapy services.

• Proven dysphagia competency and experience managing complex swallowing difficulties.

• Experience supporting stroke and neurological rehabilitation caseloads.

• Knowledge of or experience of VFSS and FEES services is highly desirable.

• Strong clinical reasoning, communication, and organizational skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

Why Choose Pulse?

From the moment you register with Pulse, our focus is entirely on you. Our specialist recruitment consultants understand your profession and are committed to finding the right opportunities to match your skills and aspirations.

With exclusive access to roles across the UK, we offer a personalized and supportive recruitment experience that puts your career first.

How to Apply

If you're interested in registering with Pulse, learning more about this role, or exploring other opportunities, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply using the link below.

Reasonable Adjustments

If you have a disability or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or within the workplace, please let us know as early as possible. We are committed to providing the support you need throughout your journey with us.

International Recruitment Notice

Please note that we are unable to accept applications from individuals residing in countries listed on the Red or Amber list of the Code of Practice for the International Recruitment of Health and Social Care Personnel in England, as defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) Workforce Support and Safeguard List.

jobs.title: Electric Propulsion Unit (EPU) Intern (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT is standing up two production lines for the first time — Squire and Viceroy — and that shift is opening up real, substantial work across our Electric Propulsion Unit (EPU) systems. As our EPU Intern, you'll sit inside the Electrical Systems team and work across the full arc of propulsion development: conceptualization, design, integration, and sustainment, across multiple platforms. You'll move fluidly between data analysis, electrical documentation, CAD, and hands-on test support, with direct exposure to motor performance evaluation, component-level testing, and on-water testing of the propulsion systems that move Seagliders through the water.

This isn't a role built around a narrow, pre-scoped task list. There's a meaningful amount of EPU work ahead of us on both Squire and Viceroy, and this internship exists to carve out a real piece of it for you to own — not to shadow, not to simulate, but to actually contribute to systems that will fly on REGENT's vehicles. You'll work alongside engineers who care about rigor as much as speed, and who'll expect you to bring your engineering fundamentals and build fast from there.

We're looking for someone who already has strong footing in electric machines, propulsion fundamentals, and CAD, and who's excited to apply that foundation to a fast-moving, dual-platform propulsion effort rather than a textbook problem set. If you want an internship where the scope is broad because the work is real, this is the seat for you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Real EPU Scope: You'll take on a defined piece of Electric Propulsion Unit work spanning both the Squire and Viceroy platforms, not a simulated side project. The work is real and waiting for someone to pick it up.

 - Evaluate Motor Performance: You'll dig into motor and drive data to characterize torque, speed, losses, and efficiency across operating conditions. This analysis directly informs decisions on both production lines.

 - Document Electrical Systems: You'll read and create schematics, wiring diagrams, and harness documentation for EPU hardware. This work unlocks your ability to interpret both vendor documentation and REGENT's own systems.

 - Build in CAD: You'll produce mechanical drawings and models in a 3D CAD environment, applying basic GD&T as you go. Your CAD work will directly support integration efforts across both platforms.

 - Support Test Campaigns: You'll get hands-on exposure to both component-level testing and on-water testing of propulsion hardware. By the midpoint of your term, you'll be comfortable with EPU layout and power distribution across current and future REGENT platforms.

 - Reduce and Interpret Data: You'll use Python, MATLAB, or Excel to process test data, build efficiency and performance models, and run mission-profile analyses. Much of the role runs through turning raw data into decisions.

 - Connect Propulsion to Power: You'll relate propeller or thruster performance — thrust, torque, advance ratio, efficiency — back to electrical input power. That connection sits at the core of how EPUs get designed and sustained here.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Engineering Fundamentals In Place: You're a rising senior or graduate student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or robotics engineering. These fundamentals are the foundation this role builds on from day one.

 - Motor and Drive Knowledge: You have working knowledge of electric machines, including BLDC/PMSM torque and speed constants, back-EMF, losses, and efficiency maps, along with motor controllers, ESCs, and basic power electronics.

 - Scripting and Data Chops: You're proficient in Python or MATLAB for processing test data and building performance models, with strong Excel skills for fast turnaround analysis. You're comfortable being the person who turns a pile of data into an answer.

 - Propulsion Fundamentals: You understand how propeller or thruster performance, including thrust, torque, advance ratio, and efficiency, relates to electrical input power. Coursework in fluid mechanics or marine or aero propulsion is a strong signal here.

 - CAD Fluency: You're proficient in a 3D CAD tool and can produce clear, accurate mechanical drawings, with a basic understanding of GD&T. That fluency will help you pick up REGENT's systems quickly.

 - Comfort With Electrical Documentation: You can read and create schematics, wiring diagrams, and harness documentation. That skill is what lets you move confidently through both vendor and REGENT engineering documentation.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Property Controls And Inventory Lead
jobs.description:
Property Controls and Inventory Lead | P1ACBRNP020

Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Product Support Integrator and Materiel Integration Support

ProSidian seeks a Property Controls and Inventory Lead to oversee Government property accountability, inventory accuracy, and custody reconciliation. The role supports a DoD acquisition environment focused on mission readiness, controlled materiel, traceability, and secure delivery.

Position details

• Employment — Full-time, W-2 exempt, with no overtime pay.
• GSA labor category — Senior Consultant I.
• Service alignment — NAICS 541611, Management and Financial Consulting, Acquisition and Grants Management Support, and Business Program and Project Management Services.
• Work arrangement — Hybrid, with work performed on and off client sites in the continental United States (CONUS).
• Workplace language — English.
• Candidate profile — Relevant DoD or military sector experience. Functional and technical expertise in property controls or inventory management is preferred.

Work locations

• Contractor operating facilities — Locations and addresses are to be determined.
• Government coordination — ACC-APG Natick, 10 General Greene Avenue, Natick, MA 01760-5011.
• Component package delivery — Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA), 10020 Kabrich Circle, Pine Bluff, AR 71602. Travel and on-site support at PBA may be required.

Responsibilities and duties

• Oversee Government materiel receipt and maintain accurate custody and location records for items in controlled storage.
• Develop cycle count plans, reconcile physical inventory against recorded balances, and investigate discrepancies.
• Track transfers and record materiel issued for kit assembly.
• Maintain required segregation and preservation controls, and keep property records ready for audit.
• Coordinate with Government supply sources and the warehouse and quality teams to reconcile records and resolve inventory issues.
• Report inventory status, forecasts, and changes that affect the integrated program schedule.

Property Controls and Inventory Lead | P1ACBRNP020

Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Product Support Integrator and Materiel Integration Support

Education and experience

• At least 5 years of experience in inventory or property control, including relevant property management experience.
• Experience managing Government-furnished property is preferred.
• An associate or bachelor’s degree in logistics or business is preferred.
• Certified Professional Property Specialist (CPPS) or Certified Professional Property Administrator (CPPA) certification is preferred where applicable.

Required skills and competencies

• Apply Government property management practices and design controls that support custody accountability.
• Use warehouse management systems (WMS) to plan cycle counts, reconcile inventory, and trace serialized assets.
• Investigate inventory discrepancies and document findings and corrective actions.
• Apply Care of Supplies in Storage (COSIS) controls to preserve stored materiel.
• Use project management methods and tools to prioritize competing tasks, meet milestones, and adapt to changing requirements.
• Demonstrate leadership, collaboration, analytical and organizational skills, and clear verbal and written communication.

Functional scope and deliverables

• Lead property control and inventory activities for CP DEPMEDS within the broader management and financial consulting, acquisition and grants management support, and business program and project management engagement.
• Coordinate with the Government source custodian, warehouse team, and Property and Item Unique Identification (IUID) Lead.
• Maintain the inventory control plan and custody records, and document inventory reconciliations.

Employment conditions

• Employment type — Full-time, regular.
• Citizenship — U.S. citizenship is required.
• Visa sponsorship — Unavailable for this position, including H-1B and TN visas.
• Background checks and drug testing — ProSidian reserves the right to require criminal history, employment, education, and licensure checks, as well as credit and motor vehicle checks where applicable. ProSidian may conduct drug testing for designated positions.
• Equal employment opportunity — ProSidian supports employee learning and professional growth and offers career opportunities across disciplines and locations.

Additional role details

• The role may oversee the Asset Management Specialist.
• The Government retains authority over release, acceptance, and disposition of Government property.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About the Role:

As a Mechanical Engineer at Motive, you will lead mechanical design and development for automotive-grade connected-device products, with a focus on connector and ruggedized waterproofing design. You will help drive NPI from early requirements and concepts through detailed design, validation, manufacturing readiness, and production ramp. You will solve technical challenges, develop prototypes and test solutions, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver products that meet product objectives and provide an exceptional customer experience.

You will bring hands-on mechanical engineering expertise, creative problem-solving, systems-integration experience, and a strong understanding of mechanical systems, design processes, tooling, and materials. You will work iteratively, adapt designs as requirements evolve, and support multiple projects across the product lifecycle.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead mechanical design and NPI execution for automotive-grade connected-device products, translating product requirements and field-use conditions into design inputs, milestones, validation plans, and production-ready hardware.

• Deliver detailed part and system design, CAD models, drawings, and design documentation from initial concept through mass production.

• Own connector and waterproofing design from concept through production, including automotive-grade connector selection or customization, terminals, retention features, cable exits, overmolds, gaskets, O-rings, vent membranes, connector caps, and ruggedized enclosure interfaces.

• Develop cable harnesses and interconnects, including wire and terminal selection, crimp requirements,material and gold plating spec, shielding, grounding, bend-radius control, strain relief, routing, retention, and supplier manufacturing requirements.

• Apply technical expertise to resolve design issues; lead failure analysis and validate corrective actions during development and for production or field failures, including connector, harness, sealing, and structural failures.

• Lead mechanical design discussions with internal and external cross-functional teams—including industrial design, EE, RF, antenna, camera, audio, manufacturing, quality, and suppliers—to make effective tradeoffs across performance, reliability, cost, and schedule.

• Manage mechanical design schedules, supplier milestones, technical risks, and issue resolution; provide hands-on support during NPI builds at manufacturing partner sites.

• Travel as needed to offshore factories to support NPI builds and production readiness, and to customer sites to investigate critical field issues and lead failure analysis (FA).

• Conduct design reviews, research materials and mechanical systems, and communicate project status and technical decisions to leadership as needed.

• Support design for manufacturability and process validation for injection-molded plastics, sheet metal, die casting, machining, and relevant joining or sealing processes.

• Create and review 2D drawings with GD&T, datum schemes, CTF dimensions, material and finish callouts, and inspection requirements. Perform tolerance stack analysis and collaborate with manufacturing/process engineering and supplier quality on CPK, FAI, SPC, and process capability.

What We’re Looking For:

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.

• Experience designing waterproof enclosures and connector interfaces for harsh environments, including sealing strategies such as gaskets, O-rings, overmolds, and cable exits, and validating designs to IP67/IP69K requirements.

• Familiarity with USCAR, SAE, ISO 16750, IEC 60529, IEC 60068, or OEM-specific requirements.

• 8+ years of experience in automotive product and mounting design, including hands-on mechanical product development and NPI.

• 8+ years of experience in product validation, including shock/drop, cycle, vibration, and environmental testing.

• 8+ years of 3D CAD experience; proficiency in Creo/Pro/ENGINEER or comparable mechanical CAD, with the ability to create production-ready 3D models and detailed 2D drawings.

• Strong working knowledge of GD&T, tolerance stack analysis, and mechanical design documentation; able to apply worst-case and statistical tolerance methods appropriately.

• Experience with thermal and structural analysis or simulation, and the ability to interpret results and apply them to design decisions.

• Knowledge of FMEA, tooling and material/process validation, including SPC, Cp, and Cpk; experience defining CTF dimensions and supporting FAI and supplier process capability.

• Strong mechanical design-for-manufacturing experience with injection-molded plastics and tooling; working knowledge of sheet metal, die casting, machining, and related supplier processes.

• Analytical problem-solving skills, including experience with 8D, Six Sigma, DOE, or similar methods.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across global, cross-functional teams.

• Ability and willingness to travel internationally to offshore manufacturing sites for NPI support and to customer sites for critical field issue investigation.

Pay Transparency
Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visiting Motive Perks & Benefits

The base compensation range for this role is:

$140,000—$190,000 USD

Creating a diverse and inclusive workplace is one of Motive's core values. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.

Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice here.

UK Candidate Privacy Notice here.

Regarding US-based roles, depending on your role and primary work location, Motive Technologies, Inc. (“Employer”) discloses candidates may be required to execute a non-compete covenant with the Employer. This requirement does not apply to lawyers, interns, or employees working in CA, MN, MT, ND, OK, or where otherwise prohibited by law.

Non-compete covenant terms in all other jurisdictions will be subject to the applicable statutory requirements, including but not limited to, procedures, industry related prohibitions, or salary and compensation thresholds.

jobs.title: Director of Dining Services
jobs.description:
• Follow Company Dining Policy and Procedures and while ensuring that all department personnel are compliant as well.
• Responsible for the purchasing of all dining food and nonfood items and ensure all purchases for the department achieve 95% DSSI ordering compliance.
• Balance and maintain budgets for raw food and supplies.

jobs.title: Gestor de Risco Não-Financeiro
jobs.description:
Assegurar uma execução eficaz e uma forte orientação operacional na implementação de processos e sistemas de Gestão do Risco Não Financeiro (NFR), enquanto elemento fundamental para a concretização dos objectivos estratégicos da organização, nas unidades de negócio e funções corporativas.

Funções Essenciais

Actuar como principal ponto de contacto em matéria de Risco Não-Financeiro (NFR) junto dos stakeholders prestando aconselhamento especializado sobre fraude, risco de informação, entre outros riscos e ameaças operacionais, de forma a apoiar a integração de mecanismos de controlo na estratégia do negócio.

Manter relações de confiança e credibilidade com as equipas de auditoria interna e externa, entidades reguladoras e instituições congéneres, promovendo uma abordagem colaborativa à supervisão e gestão do risco.

Realizar a Auto-Avaliação de Riscos e Controlos (Risk and Control Self-Assessment – RCSA) em todas as áreas de negócio aplicáveis, avaliando os diferentes tipos de risco relevantes, com vista à identificação e ao registo de fragilidades nos mecanismos de controlo.

Analisar os impactos no negócio e facilitar o processo formal de aceitação do risco nas situações em que o risco residual exceda o apetite pelo risco definido, permitindo uma tomada de decisão informada por parte da gestão.

Promover uma cultura sólida de risco e controlo nas diferentes áreas funcionais, participando em iniciativas de partilha de conhecimento que reforcem a importância da gestão do risco junto dos colaboradores.

Realizar análises detalhadas de cenários de risco, através da recolha e interpretação de dados, preparando as unidades de negócio para potenciais falhas sistémicas ou operacionais.

Contribuir para a gestão dos Riscos Não-Financeiros, identificando insuficiências ou falhas nos processos internos, nas pessoas e/ou nos sistemas, bem como riscos decorrentes de acontecimentos externos, em estruturas operacionais complexas, considerando as interdependências entre os 17 tipos de risco abrangidos pelo Risco Operacional.

Monitorizar as perdas efectivas face ao apetite pelo risco estabelecido, através da análise de dados financeiros e da elaboração de relatórios de tendências, de forma a desencadear as intervenções necessárias por parte da gestão.

Facilitar a análise das causas-raiz de incidentes relevantes de risco operacional e de informação, com o objectivo de prevenir a sua recorrência e reforçar o ambiente global de controlo.

Identificar iniciativas de elevado risco e implementações de soluções em cloud, através da utilização de ferramentas de avaliação de risco, protegendo a organização contra ameaças tecnológicas e operacionais emergentes.

Realizar avaliações de risco que acrescentem valor aos projectos estratégicos de transformação e ao lançamento de novos produtos, assegurando que as alterações ao perfil de risco do negócio são devidamente quantificadas e mitigadas.

Colaborar com a equipa de Gestão de Risco de Terceiros (Third-Party Risk Management – TPRM) na supervisão do ciclo de vida dos fornecedores e na avaliação crítica da adequação dos mecanismos de controlo associados a entidades externas, de forma a mitigar os riscos da cadeia de fornecimento.

Prestar orientação sobre a implementação das políticas de risco de informação aconselhando sobre os principais activos de informação e as fragilidades dos mecanismos de controlo, com vista à protecção da confidencialidade e integridade dos dados do Banco.

Participar nos Comités de Risco e Controlo do Negócio (Business Risk Control Committees – BRCC), disponibilizando informação factual e escalando situações relevantes, de forma a promover a responsabilização e a clara atribuição da gestão dos riscos identificados.

Utilizar as funcionalidades da plataforma Risk Market Place (RMP) para optimizar as capacidades de prestação de serviços de risco (Risk-as-a-Service) e melhorar a eficiência dos processos de reporte e monitorização do risco.

Executar decisões e intervenções de Gestão do Risco Não-Financeiro (NFR), sustentadas na análise de dados, nas diferentes linhas de negócio.

Implementar, com sentido de urgência, medidas proactivas de gestão das principais exposições ao Risco Não-Financeiro, incluindo riscos existentes e emergentes.

Apoiar a adopção dos princípios de modelização de capital, através de iniciativas de formação que permitam aos parceiros de negócio compreender as implicações das exposições ao risco operacional nos requisitos de capital.

Coordenar com as equipas de Controlo de Crime Financeiro do Grupo e de Gestão do Risco de Informação do Grupo, recorrendo ao conhecimento especializado destas áreas antes da implementação de medidas de controlo complexas.

Prestar aconselhamento sobre a aplicação das normas PCI DSS e da regulamentação relativa à privacidade de dados, seguindo os critérios estabelecidos para prevenir violações de dados e assegurar a conformidade regulamentar.

Assegurar a actualidade e relevância do modelo de Gestão do Risco Não-Financeiro (NFR), avaliando a sua eficácia e recomendando alterações em função dos riscos e ameaças emergentes.

Monitorizar e avaliar a cultura de Risco Não-Financeiro (NFR) pretendida nas três linhas de defesa, através da utilização de indicadores e mecanismos de incentivo adequados.

Prestar orientação às áreas de negócio em matéria de risco de informação, identificando os principais activos de informação, eventos de risco e respectivas causas, bem como apoiando a definição de medidas de tratamento do risco, de forma a assegurar a mitigação das fragilidades significativas e o reporte adequado dos riscos e deficiências de controlo relevantes.

Manter-se actualizado relativamente às alterações regulamentares e aos requisitos de conformidade, através da interacção e colaboração contínuas com os principais stakeholders, nomeadamente as áreas de Segurança de Tecnologias de Informação, Governação de Dados, Gestão de Acessos Lógicos (LAM), Conformidade com as normas da Indústria de Cartões de Pagamento (PCI) e Privacidade de Dados.

Apoiar a implementação e consolidação do modelo de Gestão do Risco Não-Financeiro (NFR) nas diferentes áreas de negócio, através de interacções regulares com os diversos níveis de liderança e gestão, promovendo a compreensão dos benefícios de uma abordagem integrada de gestão do risco que contemple os 17 tipos de risco.

Habilitações Literárias: Licenciatura

Área de Formação: Gestão de Empresas e Comércio, Gestão de Risco

Experiência Requerida

Gestão do Risco Operacional

Risco e Assuntos Corporativos

3-4 anos

Experiência prática na aplicação de modelos de gestão de risco e controlo no sector dos serviços financeiros.

Conhecimento aprofundado dos conceitos de apetite pelo risco, resposta ao risco e melhoria contínua de processos.

Compreensão das características do Risco Não-Financeiro e dos riscos associados ao reporte financeiro.

3-4 anos

Conhecimentos práticos dos modelos de risco e controlo e da sua aplicação no sector dos serviços financeiros.

Domínio dos conceitos de apetite pelo risco, estratégias de resposta ao risco e melhoria de processos, bem como compreensão das características do Risco Não-Financeiro e dos riscos associados ao reporte financeiro.

Competências Comportamentais

• Comunicação e apresentação clara de informações;
• Capacidade de questionar e desafiar ideias de forma construtiva;
• Capacidade de persuasão e influência;
• Adaptação e abertura à mudança;
• Análise e avaliação crítica de informações;
• Exploração de novas possibilidades;
• Criatividade e geração de ideias;
• Interpretação de dados;
• Capacidade de tomada de decisão;
• Capacidade de fornecer análises e recomendações;
• Gestão e resolução de conflitos;
• Cumprimento e promoção de normas e padrões estabelecidos.

Competências Técnicas

• Análise de riscos seguráveis;
• Gestão de capital económico;
• Avaliação da eficácia da gestão do risco;
• Identificação de riscos;
• Mensuração e avaliação de riscos;
• Elaboração de relatórios de risco;
• Definição de estratégias de resposta ao risco;
• Avaliação da relação entre risco e benefício

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About The Role

Samsara’s mission is to improve industrial efficiency, safety, and quality at a massive scale, through the use of sensors and software. Our suite of IoT products and software platform brings the benefits of sensor data to traditional industries like transportation, food and beverage distribution, construction, state and local government, and K-12 education. We help our customers transport food, medicine, and other goods safely across the country, monitor deliveries for unsafe conditions, and help fleet managers improve the efficiency of their operations.

Samsara’s Product Design team is responsible for crafting user-friendly features, workflows, and interfaces that our customers use every day to run their operations. This involves talking to customers, working with engineers and product managers to understand problems, rapidly designing and iterating on mocks and user flows, and communicating ideas effectively to stakeholders. We also build design systems that underpin all our products to ensure a consistent and cohesive user experience.

We’re looking for an experienced product design director who will build out an already high-caliber group of designers and help shape the product experience for all our customers.

This is a remote position based in the United States. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

In this role, you will:

• Lead, grow, coach and mentor a team of design managers

• Engage with customers to deeply understand their operations and people

• Ship high-quality designs based on these customer needs

• Collaborate with partners to define opportunities and deliver a best-in-class experiences

• Define and drive the product design strategy across product areas

• Create and refine tools, systems and processes that improve team health and output

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

• Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 4-6 years (or more) of product design management experience

• Strong portfolio that showcases ability to lead teams that ship elegant solutions to complex problems

An ideal candidate also has:

• Track record of shipping step-changes to the UX that drive customer and business impact

• A history of hiring, growing and retaining great talent

• Proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional partners to ship high quality experiences

• Experience identifying and instituting changes that improve employee experiences

• Expertise in providing feedback that accelerates career growth and improves product quality

• A desire to improve yourself, the team, and product experiences

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.
