jobs.title: Director, Sales and Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
Fairmarkit is the #1 autonomous sourcing platform revolutionizing the way all organizations buy & sell. Fairmarkit equips procurement teams with automation, AI, and GenAI so they can source more competitively at scale. Our solutions for tail spend and strategic sourcing help innovative procurement teams reduce cycle times, drive out costs, meet ESG/Diversity targets, and provide a better stakeholder experience to internal partners and suppliers. Fairmarkit has been recognized with awards by organizations such as Gartner and IDC, and is backed by strategic investors like Notable Capital, Insight Partners, 1984.VC, and Newfund.

Role Overview

We’re looking for a strategic, hands-on Director of Sales & Marketing Operations to lead the systems, processes, and insights that improve sales and marketing performance. You’ll own the operational framework across the full acquisition funnel—from account and prospect targeting, campaign engagement, and lead generation through pipeline creation, opportunity progression, and closed-won revenue.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Business Development, Deal Desk, and Finance leadership to align priorities, improve execution, and build scalable ways of working. You’ll establish clear attribution and measurement frameworks that connect sales and marketing activity to pipeline and revenue, helping leaders make informed investment decisions.

You’ll bring an AI-native approach to operations, embedding AI and automation into how we design workflows, generate insights, and create capacity. Success requires someone who can set direction, influence stakeholders, lead change, and stay close to execution.  This role will have one direct report and will align directly with the CFOO.

Key Responsibilities

Sales & Marketing Operations Leadership

• Set and lead the Sales and Marketing Operations strategy, translating company priorities into a roadmap that improves pipeline generation, sales productivity, and revenue performance.

• Advise Sales, Marketing, and Business Development leaders on operational priorities, investment decisions, and opportunities to improve execution.

• Establish shared performance expectations, decision-making frameworks, and accountability across Sales and Marketing.

• Lead cross-functional change, building alignment among stakeholders and resolving competing priorities to deliver measurable business outcomes.

• Anticipate operational needs as the business scales and proactively evolve processes, systems, and capabilities.

Full Funnel Operations & Attribution

• Define and own the operational framework across the full acquisition funnel—from account and prospect targeting through closed-won revenue.

• Establish consistent funnel definitions, qualification criteria, routing logic, and handoff expectations that align Sales, Marketing, and Business Development.

• Lead the attribution strategy, connecting marketing campaigns and sales activities to pipeline and revenue to measure ROI and guide investment decisions.

• Guide investment and prioritization decisions through analysis of campaign effectiveness, acquisition efficiency, conversion, and funnel velocity.

• Identify systemic barriers to performance and lead initiatives that improve pipeline quality, conversion rates, and sales cycle efficiency.

Sales Performance & Planning

• Lead the operational framework for pipeline management and forecasting, strengthening predictability and informing Sales leadership decisions and financial planning.

• Enhance performance scorecards and leadership review cadences that translate insights into decisions, clear ownership, and action.

• Partner with Finance and Sales leadership to maintain impactful sales commission plans that align incentives with strategic initiatives and business goals.

• Lead territory, coverage, and capacity strategy in partnership with Sales leadership, aligning organizational design and resource investment with market opportunity and long-term growth objectives.

Sales & Marketing Systems Strategy

• Set the sales and marketing technology strategy and roadmap, balancing business needs, scalability, cost, and adoption.

• Lead the design and evolution of integrations across Salesforce and connected platforms to enable reliable data flow and effective workflows.

• Establish standards for system design, access, documentation, and change management in coordination with other system stakeholders.

• Evaluate technology investments against measurable business value, driving adoption and consolidating or replacing tools where appropriate.

AI-Native Operations & Transformation

• Define and lead an AI-native approach to Sales and Marketing Operations, making AI and automation core to how work is designed and delivered.

• Build and prioritize a portfolio of AI and automation initiatives that improve team capacity, campaign execution, lead prioritization, and sales productivity.

• Lead experimentation from initial use case through implementation and adoption, with clear measures of quality, efficiency, and business impact.

• Recommend workflow (re)design to capture the benefits of AI and automation, challenging existing processes and simplifying how teams work.

• Influence leaders and users to adopt new capabilities, establishing practical standards for responsible use, output validation, and ongoing improvement.

Data Strategy, Insights & Enablement

• Establish the sales and marketing measurement framework, aligning leaders on trusted metrics, data definitions, and ownership.

• Own the quality and reliability of sales and marketing data, addressing root causes and establishing sustainable governance.

• Deliver executive-level insights that explain performance, surface emerging risks and opportunities, and recommend action.

• Set the reporting and analytics roadmap, prioritizing visibility that improves decisions and accountability.

• Recommend enablement and adoption strategies that embed systems, processes, and insights into how Sales and Marketing operate.

Qualifications

• 10+ years of progressive experience in Sales Operations, Marketing Operations, or related roles in B2B SaaS, including experience setting operational direction and leading cross-functional initiatives.

• Demonstrated ownership across both sales and marketing operations, with full-funnel experience spanning pre-pipeline activity through closed-won revenue.

• Proven expertise in campaign measurement, attribution models, funnel analytics, and connecting sales and marketing investments to pipeline and revenue outcomes.

• Strong systems expertise, with experience shaping technology strategy and designing scalable platforms, integrations, and automation.

• Experience managing marketing automation, sales engagement, data enrichment, forecasting, and reporting platforms.

• Demonstrated use of AI and automation to improve workflows, with sound judgment around data quality, output validation, and adoption.

• Strong analytical skills, including proficiency with Excel/Google Sheets, dashboard development, and translating complex data into clear recommendations.

• Ability to influence leaders, align stakeholders, and lead change across teams without relying on direct authority.

• A strategic perspective paired with the willingness and technical ability to build, troubleshoot, and execute.

• Excellent communication, prioritization, and project leadership skills in a remote, fast-paced environment.

Remote work opportunities may be limited to designated states. The compensation range for this position is $162,000 - $245,000 (including bonus) + equity, and benefits. This range is provided in accordance with applicable U.S. pay transparency laws. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and location. #LI-remote #LI-YM1

Headquartered in Boston, and backed by a $35.6M Series C co-led by OMERS, Highland, Notable Capital, Insight Partners, and ServiceNow. We are looking for exceptional candidates who want to help grow our company into a global enterprise and make their mark on the B2B tech industry. Come soar to new heights with us!

jobs.title: Intern, Field Service Engineer
jobs.description:
Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture. ​

For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving.  But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world.  Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential.

As a Field Service Engineer Intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting advanced semiconductor equipment while learning how engineers help customers keep complex manufacturing systems operating safely and reliably.

Based at our customer site in Hillsboro, Oregon, this internship gives you the opportunity to put your engineering education into practice in a high-tech semiconductor manufacturing environment. You’ll work alongside experienced Field Service Engineers, receive hands-on training and mentorship, and contribute to real technical projects and equipment-support activities.

Throughout the internship, you’ll gain exposure to technologies such as vacuum systems, plasma, chemical delivery, robotics, sensors, advanced metrology, electrical and mechanical systems, and complex hardware-software interactions.

You’ll also have a defined internship project with clear objectives and deliverables, allowing you to apply your technical knowledge to a real engineering challenge. At the conclusion of the internship, you’ll have the opportunity to present your project, results, and key learnings to the team.

What You’ll Be Working On

• Work alongside experienced Field Service Engineers to support the installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and performance of semiconductor equipment.

• Gain hands-on experience with complex mechanical, electrical, vacuum, robotics, sensor, and control systems.

• Assist with troubleshooting equipment issues using structured problem-solving techniques and guidance from experienced engineers.

• Participate in equipment inspections, testing, diagnostics, and other engineering support activities.

• Learn how engineers use schematics, procedures, technical documentation, equipment data, and diagnostic tools to identify technical issues.

• Work in a semiconductor cleanroom environment while following established safety, quality, and customer requirements.

• Support continuous improvement projects focused on equipment reliability, serviceability, safety, and efficiency.

• Gain exposure to how Field Service Engineers collaborate with customers, process engineers, product teams, and other technical organizations.

• Develop technical documentation and summarize findings, observations, and project results.

• Complete a defined internship project addressing a real equipment, service, reliability, or engineering challenge.

• Participate in team meetings, technical discussions, training, and professional-development opportunities.

• Present your internship project and key learnings at the conclusion of the program.

What We’re Looking For

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electromechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Interest in semiconductor equipment, advanced manufacturing, robotics, automation, or complex electromechanical systems.

• Hands-on experience gained through coursework, labs, research, student projects, engineering clubs, previous internships, or personal technical projects.

• Basic ability to read and interpret electrical, electronic, or electromechanical schematics.

• Strong problem-solving skills and an eagerness to learn how complex systems operate.

• Comfortable working in a hands-on, fast-paced technical environment.

• Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment and follow established safety procedures.

• Strong communication and teamwork skills.

• Curiosity and willingness to ask questions, receive feedback, and learn from experienced engineers.

• Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

What Sets You Apart

You don't need to check every box. Relevant experience can come from coursework, labs, research, student organizations, competitions, personal projects, or previous internships.

• Exposure to semiconductor manufacturing or wafer fabrication.

• Coursework or projects involving robotics, automation, vacuum technology, electronics, mechanical systems, controls, plasma, or gas-delivery systems.

• Experience using basic electrical or mechanical diagnostic and test equipment.

• Previous internship, co-op, research, senior design, or hands-on engineering project experience.

• Experience developing technical reports, engineering documentation, or project presentations.

• Participation in engineering clubs, robotics teams, Formula SAE, IEEE, maker organizations, or similar technical activities.

• Interest in data analysis, statistical methods, and structured problem solving.

• Previous experience working in a team-oriented or customer-facing environment.

• A strong commitment to safety, quality, and continuous learning.

What You’ll Gain From the Internship

During the internship, you’ll have the opportunity to:

• Apply your engineering education to real semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

• Gain hands-on experience working with complex electromechanical systems and advanced technology.

• Receive mentorship and technical guidance from experienced Field Service Engineers.

• Build practical troubleshooting and diagnostic skills.

• Learn how electrical, mechanical, software, controls, robotics, vacuum, and process technologies work together within semiconductor equipment.

• Gain exposure to the day-to-day responsibilities of a Field Service Engineer.

• Experience working within a semiconductor fab and cleanroom environment.

• Develop your technical communication, teamwork, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

• Build relationships with engineers and other professionals across the organization.

• Explore potential career paths in Field Service, Equipment Engineering, Process Engineering, Product Support, Technical Operations, and other engineering functions.

• Complete a meaningful technical project that you can discuss as part of your professional experience.

• Present your work and accomplishments at the end of the internship.

The Internship Experience

This internship is designed to provide more than observation. You’ll be part of the engineering team and have opportunities to learn, contribute, troubleshoot, collaborate, and solve real technical problems with guidance from experienced engineers.

Your experience will combine:

• Hands-on technical learning

• Mentorship from experienced engineers

• A defined engineering project

• Exposure to advanced semiconductor manufacturing

• Cross-functional collaboration

• Professional and technical skill development

• A final project presentation

By the end of the internship, you’ll have a stronger understanding of semiconductor equipment, field engineering, troubleshooting, and the technical disciplines that come together to make advanced semiconductor manufacturing possible.

Why Join ASM?

If you enjoy taking things apart, understanding how complex systems work, solving technical problems, and learning by doing, this internship gives you the opportunity to apply those interests in one of the world’s most advanced technology industries.

At ASM, you’ll gain exposure to the equipment and engineering behind semiconductor manufacturing while learning from experienced professionals in the field. You’ll have an opportunity to build practical engineering skills, strengthen your technical foundation, and explore whether a career in Field Service Engineering and the semiconductor industry is right for you.

Your internship is an opportunity to learn, contribute, build connections, and experience firsthand how engineering helps enable the technology behind AI and other next-generation applications.

Apply today to be part of what’s next.

We make the tech that enables the chips in devices which improve lives around the world. We do this with an eye to the future, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible through cutting-edge innovation, and driving the next wave of technological breakthroughs that shape how we live, work, and connect.

To learn more about ASM, find us at asm.com and on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

jobs.description:

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. · Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Standing

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Orientation and training provided on the job.

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

Standing

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Delivery Expert(04467) - Lewes, DE
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? We mean that we offer a great flexible schedule that offers the hours you're looking for. That means you're free when you need to be. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, to hang with your friends, or whatever. Even if you need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Intern, Process Engineering
jobs.description:
Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture. ​

For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving.  But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world.  Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential.

As a Process Engineer Intern at ASM, you will gain hands-on experience working with advanced semiconductor processing and analytical equipment while supporting the research, development, and optimization of processes used in semiconductor manufacturing.

During this internship, you may gain exposure to technologies such as Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD/PEALD), Epitaxy, PECVD, oxidation, annealing, and curing for applications across logic, memory, analog, power, and MEMS devices.

Working alongside experienced process engineers and technical teams, you will contribute to a defined project, participate in experiments, analyze process and materials data, and learn how advanced thin-film processes are developed and optimized. This internship is designed to provide meaningful technical experience while allowing you to apply concepts from your academic studies in a real-world semiconductor environment.

Responsibilities

• Support process engineers in the research, development, and optimization of semiconductor processes, including ALD, PEALD, Epitaxy, PECVD, oxidation, annealing, and/or curing.

• Assist with the design and execution of experiments to evaluate process performance, materials properties, and equipment capabilities.

• Collect, analyze, and interpret experimental data with guidance from experienced engineers.

• Gain exposure to Design of Experiments (DOE) and other structured problem-solving methodologies used in semiconductor process development.

• Support thin-film development and characterization for emerging semiconductor applications.

• Work hands-on with semiconductor processing and analytical equipment in a laboratory or cleanroom environment.

• Assist with troubleshooting process and equipment-related challenges using scientific problem-solving methods.

• Gain experience with materials characterization techniques such as XPS, SIMS, AFM, XRR, XRD, TEM, SEM, and ellipsometry, depending on project needs and available equipment.

• Collaborate with process engineering, equipment engineering, applications, and other technical teams.

• Document experimental procedures, results, observations, and conclusions.

• Participate in technical discussions and learn how process results are translated into solutions for semiconductor applications.

• Complete a defined internship project aligned with ASM's process development or technology objectives.

• Prepare and deliver a final technical presentation summarizing your project, results, key learnings, and recommendations.

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Master’s, or PhD in:

• Chemical Engineering

• Materials Science or Materials Engineering

• Electrical Engineering

• Chemistry

• Physics

• Or a closely related technical field

• Interest in semiconductor manufacturing, thin-film deposition, materials science, or process engineering.

• Academic, laboratory, research, or project experience related to semiconductor processing, materials, chemistry, or engineering.

• Basic understanding of experimental design, data analysis, and scientific problem-solving.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work collaboratively within a technical team.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and gain hands-on experience in semiconductor process development.

Preferred Qualifications

• Coursework, research, or laboratory experience involving ALD, CVD, PECVD, Epitaxy, oxidation, annealing, thin films, plasma processing, or related semiconductor processes.

• Familiarity with materials characterization techniques such as XPS, SIMS, RBS, AFM, XRR, XRD, TEM, SEM, or ellipsometry.

• Exposure to Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, or experimental data analysis.

• Basic understanding of semiconductor devices, CMOS technology, or semiconductor fabrication processes.

• Experience working in a university laboratory, research group, cleanroom, or similar technical environment.

• Exposure to computational modeling, data analysis, or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is a plus.

• Interest in developing a career in the semiconductor equipment or advanced manufacturing industry.

What You'll Gain

• Hands-on experience with advanced semiconductor process development.

• Exposure to ALD, Epitaxy, PECVD, thin films, and materials characterization.

• Experience applying classroom and research knowledge to real-world semiconductor engineering challenges.

• Mentorship and guidance from experienced process engineers and technical experts.

• Experience working with experimental data, DOE methodologies, and semiconductor processing equipment.

• Exposure to the relationship between materials, process conditions, equipment, and semiconductor device performance.

• Experience collaborating across technical disciplines in a global semiconductor technology environment.

• A meaningful technical project that you can present at the conclusion of your internship.

Internship Details

Internship Status: This position is specifically designed as a student internship. Candidates should be actively enrolled in an accredited degree program during the internship period or meet ASM's applicable internship eligibility requirements.

Work Environment: Depending on the assignment, interns may perform hands-on work in laboratory, cleanroom, and semiconductor processing environments and will be expected to follow all applicable safety and operational requirements.

Apply today to be part of what’s next.

We make the tech that enables the chips in devices which improve lives around the world. We do this with an eye to the future, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible through cutting-edge innovation, and driving the next wave of technological breakthroughs that shape how we live, work, and connect.

To learn more about ASM, find us at asm.com and on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

ASM is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, nationality, social or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identify or expression, marital status, pregnancy, political affiliation, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES Shift Lead (7527)
jobs.location: West Valley City, UT, United States
jobs.description:
We are looking for future managers! Do you want to manage your future?

You were born to be the boss. We know. You get up in the morning and you make sure everyone else in the house is doing what they need to do. Then you go to work, and you make sure that everyone there is doing what they need to do, even your boss. You just do that because you've always done it. Well maybe it's time you moved up. You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance - Domino's is hiring bosses - more specifically store managers or as we like to call you Assistant Manager. Be the second in command of a million-dollar business. Grow to become THE boss. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills - judgment, leadership, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

This is a full-time, hourly position, with overtime available. Oversee all aspects of the store.  Haven't managed people before? Great, we will show you how to lead. Haven't made pizzas before? Great we'll teach you how to make an awesome pizza. You may be asked to help at other locations near to your chosen location.

This position is 5+ days per week, most weekends.

You are accountable for everything that happens within your store. Whether People, Operations, Sales, or Profits. This includes ensuring the safety, training, and culture of your team. You will lead by example because your team will follow every example you give. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

Allow us to text you when you apply! No one answers a call from someone they don't know, let us text you to start the conversation.

What we offer:

• A safe, rewarding, and fast-paced working environment
• Competitive hourly rate and benefits package
• Training with an industry-leading brand
• Excellent career opportunities
• Awesome discounts on menu items!

• 18+ years of age
• Good driving record
• Great positive attitude
• High Energy
• Prior experience in Domino's OR prior experience leading people
• Ability to use MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook
• High School diploma or equivalent
• Good background check
• Eligible to work in the USA
• Currently residing in the Salt Lake City area

• Weekly paychecks
• Bonus paid monthly for managers
• Additional periodic bonuses available
• Mileage paid daily if delivering
• Paid vacation
• Health, Dental, and Vision after 90 days
• IRA with company match after one year

We will handle your privacy and data in accordance with EEOC guidelines.

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From assistant manager to general manager, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

jobs.title: Assistant Manager (04141) - 3300 Buford Highway
jobs.description:
Overview:

Welcome to Domino's Pizza! Do you want to be an Assistant Manager? Here at Domino's, we want you to have a real career! As an Assistant Manager, you will go through four progressive stages in managing. As we teach and you learn, you'll get promoted and receive an increase in your hourly pay — all the way until you are ready to supervise your very own store!

All Assistant managers will have:

• Weekly pay
• FREE access to board-certified physicians after 30 days of employment
• Management training and to move up and become a store manager
• Flexible Schedules
• Employee Discounts

Duties & Responsibilities:

Assistant managers are responsible for everything during the shift, including cost control, inventory control, cash control, and customer relations.

Your job responsibilities would include (but are not limited to):

• Perform all the duties of the Customer Services Representatives and Delivery Drivers.
• Manage anywhere from 3 to 30 employees during your scheduled shift.
• Be responsible for all store operations.
• Greeting customers and taking orders with a smile (yes, you even have to smile when you answer the phone)!
• Operating the cash register and collecting payments from customers.
• Making fast, accurate, and consistent products that comply with all portion sizes, recipes, and baking procedures.
• Delivering product by vehicle from the store to the customer safely and courteously.
• Maintaining cleanliness of the restaurant from the first thing the customer sees to the back of the store.
• Maintain a professional appearance at all times in compliance with the Domino's Pizza Grooming Standards.

Requirements:

The good news is we can teach you how to answer the phone and make a perfect pizza. But here are a few skills you should have to be a successful Assistant Manager:

• Experience leading a team; you will manage a staff of anywhere from 3 to 30 people during your shift.
• A clean driving record and the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Record check.
• Valid Drivers License
• Access to reliable transportation.
• Full open availability.
• You have to be at least 18 years old.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

You'll have plenty of time left over for school, hanging with your friends, or whatever. Sound good? Even if you just need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

We are searching for qualified customer service reps with personality and people skills. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, drop us a line. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

• You must be 18 years of age or older.

GENERAL JOB DUTIES FOR ALL TEAM MEMBERS

• Operate all equipment.
• Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
• Prepare product.
• Receive and process telephone orders.
• Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
• Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training
Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

• Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
• Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

• Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
• Must be able to make correct monetary change.
• Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
• Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
• Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS
Exposure to:

• Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
• In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
• Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
• Fumes from food odors.
• Exposure to cornmeal dust.
• Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
• Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
• Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

• Talking and hearing on telephone.
• Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
• Depth perception.
• Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS
The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

Additional Job Details

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Including, but not limited to the following:
Standing

• Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

• For short distances for short durations.
• Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

• Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

• Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
• Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
• Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

• Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
• Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
• Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

• To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
• Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

• Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

• Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
• Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
• Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
• Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

• Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

• Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
• Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
• Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
• Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

• Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
• Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
• Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
• Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
• Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
• Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

• Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

ADVANCEMENT
Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From customer service representative to management, General Manager to Manager Corporate Operations or Franchisee, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY
Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT
We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age or older

General job duties for all store team members

• Have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

• You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

• Operate all equipment.

• Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

• Prepare product.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

• Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

• Must be able to make correct monetary change.

• Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

• Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

• Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

• Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

• In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

• Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

• Fumes from food odors.

• Exposure to cornmeal dust.

• Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

• Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

• Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

• Talking and hearing on telephone.

• Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

• Depth perception.

• Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

• Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

• Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing walking and climbing duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to thefollowing:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

• Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

• Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

• Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

• Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

• Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

• Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

• To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24- 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

• Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

• Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

• Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

• Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

• Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

• Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

• Workers reach above 72occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

• Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

• Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

• Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

• Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

• Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

• Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

• Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

• Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

• Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

• Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

• Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

• Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the
phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTSincluding, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile"bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72"high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24"- 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72"occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.
Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing"walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Ground Station Platform
jobs.description:
About the role

Muon is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our team and help scale our core platforms. In this role, you'll design foundational architecture, ship customer-facing features with real, immediate impact, and tackle a wide range of complex technical challenges.

You'll work within a tight-knit team that values open communication, cross-functional collaboration, and moving quickly without cutting corners. You'll partner closely with other engineering teams to translate business needs into reliable, well-crafted solutions. Whether you're building something from scratch or improving what already exists, you'll have a direct hand in shaping the systems our customers depend on every day.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and evolve high-performance systems that are scalable, resilient, and reliable.

• Work across the stack, and cross-functionally to deliver end-to-end platform capabilities.

• Contribute to architectural decisions that shape the long-term direction of our core systems.

• Identify and resolve bottlenecks, performance issues, and systemic risks in production environments.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business and product needs into well-crafted technical solutions.

• Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, and knowledge sharing across teams.

• Take ownership of features from concept through deployment and ongoing operation.

Qualifications

• BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field OR equivalent industry experience.

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Rust, in production environments.

• Experience in distributed systems, backend services, or platform development.

• Demonstrated experience building and operating mission-critical services with uptime, reliability, and performance requirements

• Knowledge of cloud-native infrastructure (e.g., containers, service orchestration, observability stacks).

• Strong debugging, profiling, and code optimization skills.

• Experience mentoring junior engineers or leading medium to large technical initiatives.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Comfort working in a highly interdisciplinary environment with engineers, operators, and domain specialists.

• Familiarity with real-time data processing pipelines or high-throughput systems.

• Experience with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, or automated deployment workflows.

• Contributions to open-source projects or a track record of technical writing and knowledge sharing.

Salary

The salary range for this role is $213,000 - $237,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.  Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Muon is currently registered and able to hire in the following states:
AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. The Company may, for legitimate business reasons, decline to pursue any export licensing process.

jobs.description:
The chief responsibility of Assistant Managers for Domino's is to provide managerial assistance to the store's General Manager in running and implementing operating standards in the restaurant. Assistant Managers must be adaptable and self-motivated, and have a passion for customer service. Domino's is looking for someone who thrives in a fast paced yet fun working environment and can help maintain a positive crew morale. Assistant Managers also have to know how to prepare pizzas and how best to deliver to designated places where the orders have been made. They also need to drop off nightly deposits and do the paperwork needed when the General Manager is not around. Cash management, people management and time management skills are all required for the position.

While performing the duties of this job, the team member may be required to work outdoors, in various temperatures, in a noisy environment, near moving mechanical parts, with dangerous equipment or sharp tools, and around fumes, odors, dust or toxic chemicals. This job can be physically demanding: the team member may be required to use hand repetitively, stand for prolonged periods, bend over, twist, reach above shoulder level, crouch or stoop or kneel.

• Counting inventory and supplies on a nightly basis
• Analyze labor and sales on a continual basis
• Ensure facility and equipment cleanliness based on company standards
• Efficient employee supervision
• Interviewing, hiring and onboarding new team members
• Preparing and packaging food products
• Cleaning and maintenance of the store and its equipment
• Rotating commissary deliveries

We will ensure you are trained and have a positive learning experience when you join our team. Starting wage for all newly hired assistant managers is based on prior experience, but generally starts out at minimum wage + $.50 with raises available based on performance reviews by the Regional Supervisors, typical in 4 week increments. Top AM pay per hour is $2.75 over Minimum Wage plus a monthly bonus, for eligible AMs, based on store and AM performance of a base starting at $100 per month.

Assistant Managers must:

• Be at least 18 years of age
• Have a minimum two years of customer service or restaurant experience preferred
• Be enthusiastic and willing to learn
• Be able to work with minimal supervision
• Be able to motivate and build solid, cohesive teams
• Have strong communication and problem solving skills
• Be customer service oriented
• Be able to work long hours, scheduled or unscheduled, which will include nights, weekends, and as emergencies arise
• Be willing to learn and be comfortable performing other workstation duties within the restaurant as needed and work the above listed duties with reasonable accommodation if needed

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Pay rate $15.95 to $19.00 hourly with bonus earning potential.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Product Design
jobs.description:
The Role

Digible is hiring a Senior Manager, Product Design to define what Product Design is at Digible. This is a player/coach role: roughly three-quarters of your time doing hands-on design across our pods as a shared design resource, and a quarter building the design function — managing and growing our Product Designer, and establishing our design principles, design ops, design system, design career ladder, and design job descriptions from first principles.

Above all, we're looking for an expert in designing data, analytics, and intelligence products: someone who takes dense performance data and makes it engaging, delightful, trustworthy, and AI-forward, so customers want to open it, understand it on their own, and act on it.

You'll be the most senior design voice in the company, partnering with product managers, engineers, agency leaders and leadership to make design a durable competitive advantage — in a company where reporting clarity, customer experience, operational excellence, data storytelling, and trust are the product. You'll lead AI transformation for the design practice, and you'll set the foundations (and the bar) that every future design hire builds on. You'll report to the VP of Product.

We're a small product org inside a profitable, bootstrapped company — nine years successful before the recent AI wave, and now in the middle of an AI transformation, reinventing how an established company operates and thrives in the AI era. Profitability and bootstrapping mean you'll work on real customer and business problems, not a search for product/market fit, with a direct line to an accessible leadership team. You'll use AI throughout your workflow to move faster and more effectively than a team our size normally could.

You'll Love This Job If You Love:

Products with…

• 📊 Data, Analytics & Intelligence: a portfolio where making data engaging, delightful, and trustworthy IS the product's competitive edge

• 🏢 Internal Products, SaaS-Level Ambition: internal agency teams as primary users today — a portfolio ready to be elevated into innovative, SaaS-quality experiences as we evolve toward serving customers directly

• ✨ AI: deciding what AI should surface, summarize, and say in front of a customer, and defining what AI-native design practice looks like for a whole company

Roles with…

• ⚖️ Player/Coach Balance: staying hands-on in the craft while building the function and the team

• 🏗️ Founding Scope: writing the design principles, design system, design ops, and design career ladder from page one

Organizations with…

• 🚀 Small Teams: working with small teams that trade scale for agility & autonomy

• 🏗️ Early Foundations: crafting the systems, rituals, and mindsets of a relatively new product org

Cultures with…

• 📅 4-day Workweek: we work Mon–Thu, so every weekend is a long weekend

• ⚖️ Modeled Balance: we know work is a part of life — boundaries are modeled by leadership

Businesses with…

• 📈 Fast Growth: this isn't a turnaround — 371% three-year growth per the 2025 Inc. 5000 (No. 1,165)

• 🥾 Bootstrapped Profitability: we control our own destiny, with no investor or burn pressure

What You'll Do:

• 🎨 Hands-On Design: carry real design work across pods as our shared, senior design resource (~75%)

• 📊 Data & Intelligence Design: set the bar for how Digible presents data, analytics, and AI-generated intelligence to customers, so every report, dashboard, and insight is engaging, delightful, trustworthy, and AI-forward

• 👥 Manage & Grow: coach and develop our Product Designer (~25% of your time, alongside function-building)

• 🧠 Product Strategy & Roadmap Partner: partner with product managers on product strategy and roadmaps, bringing design's point of view on customer problems and experience to what we build and why, not just how it looks

• 🔍 Customer Research Leader: lead how Digible runs customer research and discovery: interview practice, our customer advisory board, and feedback analysis and synthesis, so customer insight shapes decisions across pods

• 🤝 Stakeholder Partnership: build relationships across pods and agency teams — internal stakeholders are design's customers and champions, not ticket-writers

• 📐 Define the Practice: establish Digible's design principles, critique culture, quality standards, design career ladder, and design job descriptions — codifying what great taste means here so quality survives AI-speed production

• 🧱 Build the Infrastructure: develop, lead, and iterate on our design system and design ops — grounded in best practices — so a small team ships like a big one

• ✨ AI-Native Function: define what an AI-native design practice looks like, build it into how we work, and lead AI transformation for design at Digible

• 📡 Design Thought Leadership: be the company's design trend expert — educate the team and leadership on where design and AI are heading

How Success Will Be Measured:

Business Metrics

• Product CSAT: product design becomes a measurable driver of customer sentiment and satisfaction

• Data Engagement: customers open, understand, and act on our data on their own, not only when an account manager walks them through it

Function Metrics

• Design System Adoption: coverage and usage of the system across shipped product

• Consistency & Quality: a coherent experience across pods, visible in audits and QA

• Team Health & Growth: your designer's development, engagement, and output trajectory

• Design Velocity: design is never the bottleneck — ops and process keep pace with eng

What You Should Have:

Must Have

• 6+ years of product design experience, including 2+ years managing or formally mentoring designers

• A standout track record designing data, analytics, or intelligence products that customers find engaging and trustworthy: dashboards, reporting, insights, AI-generated summaries, or similar. This is the core of the role

• Player/coach by choice: still excellent (and happy) doing hands-on design ~75% of the time

• Built design foundations from scratch — principles, design system, ops, or critique culture from scratch — with the taste to define what "great" means

• AI-forward design practice: hands-on with AI tools and opinionated about where they fit in the craft

• Comfortable leading through ambiguity with minimal infrastructure and incomplete information

Preferred

• Start-up to scale-up (50-200 people) experience

• First-design-leader or founding-designer experience

• Experience designing AI features customers rely on (summaries, recommendations, conversational interfaces) and the trust and explainability patterns around them

Bonus

• Digital marketing domain knowledge

• Real estate domain knowledge (ex: rentals, multifamily, single family, etc.)

This role is open to candidates located within the United States.

While this job description outlines the core expectations of the role, it’s not a full list of everything you’ll do at Digible. We believe in leaning in by hitting your key goals, sharing insights, and finding new ways to elevate performance, process, and client success.

Pay, Perks and More!

• Salary Range: $160k - $190k annually

• 4-Day Work Week (32 Hour Work Week)

• WFA (Work From Anywhere) OR 1 Day / Week Remote

• Discretionary Bonus

• We offer 3 weeks of PTO as well as Sick leave, and Bereavement.

• We offer 11 paid holidays! (not counting ones that fall on Friday!)

• 401(k) + Match

• 75% Employer Paid Health Benefits (Medical, Dental, and Vision)

• Mental and Physical Wellness Reimbursement Benefit

• $1000/year travel fund for employees who have been with Digible 3+ years

• Paid Parental Leave

• Dog-Friendly Office

• Monthly Social Events

• Weekly lunches and snacks for in office employees!

HEADS UP! We believe in transparency throughout our hiring process. To help us ensure a great fit, we'll ask you to share a few professional references during the hiring process who can speak to your experience and skills. It’s all part of our commitment to open, honest communication and our core values: Focus, Authenticity, Humility, Curiosity, and Happiness.
